src: Replacement of SAFARI-1 nuclear research reactor Cabinet approved the setting up of the multi-purpose nuclear reactor project to replace the current SAFARI-1 nuclear research reactor owned by the South African Nuclear Energy Corporation (NECSA).
tgt: Go Tsenywa ga Reekthara ye Nngwe ya Dinyakišišo tša Nyutleleara ya SAFARI-1 Kabinete e dumeletše go hlongwa ga protšeke ya reekthara ya nyutleleara ya mešomo ye mentši ka nepo ya go tšeela legato reekthara ya bjale ya nyutleleara ya SAFARI-1 yeo e lego ya Koporase ya Enetši ya Nyutleleara ya Afrika Borwa (NECSA).

src: The reactor has been in operation from 1965 and its lifespan is due to end in 2030.
tgt: Reekthara ye e thomile go šoma ka 1965 gomme nako ya yona ya go šoma e tlo fela ka 2030.

src: SAFARI-1 is one of the four leading producers of medical radioisotopes in the world used to treat millions of patients annually.
tgt: SAFARI-1 ke ye nngwe ya batšweletši ba bane bao ba etilego pele ba radioaesothopu ya tša kalafo lefaseng yeo e šomišwago go alafa dimilione tša balwetši ngwaga o mongwe le o mongwe.

src: It also provides the country with support in science research, development and innovation in medicine, agriculture, paleontology and bioscience.
tgt: E thekga naga gape le mo dinyakišišong tša mahlale, mo legorong la go dira dihlare, mo boleming, mo dithutong tša masaledi batho le diphoofolo le mo mahlaleng a tša tlhago.

src: The replacement will ensure South Africa remains one of the leading countries in these fields and benefit from the new technologies in this environment.
tgt: Go tsenywa ga reekthara ye mpsha go tla netefatša gore Afrika Borwa e tšwela pele go ba ye nngwe ya dinaga tše di etilego pele ka mo Makaleng a le gore e holege go ditheknolotši tše diswa ka mo lefapheng le.

src: The project will be led by a number of related departments and NECSA as the main client.
tgt: Protšeke ye e tla etwa pele ke dikgoro tše mmalwa tše di amanego le NECSA bjalo ka modirelwamogolo.

src: South Africa’s 4th Biennial Update Report.
tgt: Pego ya Bone ya Naga ya Afrika Borwa ka ga Tshedimošo ya Moragorago ye e Ntšhiwago ka Morago ga Dingwaga tše Pedi.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the country’s 4th Biennial Update Report – which provides an update on the country’s efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change – to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go romelwa ga Pego ya Bone ya Naga ya Afrika Borwa ka ga Tshedimošo ya Moragorago ye e Ntšhiwago ka Morago ga Dingwaga tše Pedi – yeo e šišinyago gore go fanwe ka tshedimošo ya moragorago ka ga matsapa a naga ye a go fokotša le go beakanya leswa phetogo ya tlelaemete – go Kopano ya Mokgatlo wa Dinagakopano ka ga Metheo ya Phetogo ya Tlelaemete (UNFCCC).

src: The report outlines the policies implemented as well as the measures and actions undertaken by the country to reduce GHG emissions.
tgt: Pego ye e hlagiša melawana yeo e phethagaditšwego gammogo le magato le ditiro tšeo di dirilwego ke naga ye ka nepo ya go fokotša meši ya GHE hlagiša gape Tshedimošo ya moragorago ka ga go fetoša ditsenogare tša go leka go fokotša meši yeo e tšweletšwago ke ditiro tša ekonomi go latela Sengwalwa sa Ditherišano sa Bosetšhaba ka ga Melawana ya go Arabela Phetogo ya Tlelaemete.

src: It also provides an update on the transitioning interventions towards a lower carbon economy guided by the National Climate Change Response Policy White Paper.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e ikgafile go tsenya letsogo ka maleba go matsapa a lefase ka bophara a go fokotša meši ya GHG go latela dintlha tša tlhabollo tšeo di beilwego pele ke naga.

src: South Africa has made a commitment to contribute fairly to the global efforts to stabilise GHG emissions within the country’s developmental priorities.
tgt: Bjalo ka mosaenedi wa UNFCCC, Afrika Borwa e emetšwe go romela dipego tše tša moragorago kgafetšakgafetša.

src: Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).
tgt: Seabe sa Maikemišetšo sa Bosetšhaba (NDC).

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s revised NDC climate change mitigation target range for 2030 for submission to the UNFCCSouth Africa has revised its target range for 2025 to 398 to 510 and for 2030 to 350 – 420 Metric tons of Carbon Dioxide equivalent (Mt Co2-eq).
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše NDC ye e bušeleditšwego ya Afrika Borwa ka ga mollwane wa dinepišo tša go fokotša phetogo ya klaemete tša 2030 go romelwa go UNFCCAfrika Borwa e bušeleditše mollwane wa nepišo ya yona ya 2025 go tloga go tše 398 go ya go tše 510 gomme tša 2030 go tloga go tše 350 go ya go tše 420 tša ditone tša Methriki tša tekano ya Khaponetaeoksaete (Mt Co2-eq).

src: Under the Paris Agreement all parties are required to deposit NDCs every five years.
tgt: Ka fase ga Tumelelano ya Paris dinaga ka moka di swanetše go romela di-NDC tša tšona kamorago ga mengwaga ye mengwe le ye mengwe ye mehlano.

src: South Africa deposited its first NDC with the UNFCCC in October 2015, committing to keep national GHG emissions within a range from 398 to 614 Mt CO2-eq for 2025 and 2030.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e rometše NDC ya yona ya mathomo go UNFCCC ka Diphalane 2015, go realo e tshepiša go fokotša meši ya GHG nageng ya yona k mollwaneng wa go tloga go 398 go fihla go 614 tša ditone tša Methriki tša tekano ya Khaponetaeoksaete ka ngwaga wa 2025 le wa 2030.

src: The Paris Agreement also seeks to lower the global temperatures to well below two degrees Celsius and pursue efforts to degrees Celsius.
tgt: Tumelelano ya Paris e nyaka gape go fokotša dithempheretšha tša lefase ka bophara go ya fase gareng ga kgrata le seripagare le dikgrata tše pedi tša Selšias.

src: All parties were expected to update their 2015 targets in 2020 to ensure they are aligned to the latest science.
tgt: Dinaga ka moka di ile tša emelwa go mpshafatša dinepišo tša tšona tša ngwaga wa 2015 ka 2020 go netefatša gore di sepelelana le dithutamahlale tša moragorago.

src: The revised target range takes into account the latest reports of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and is aligned with all the stakeholders that contribute towards the country’s efforts.
tgt: Mellwane ya dinepišo ye e bušeleditšwego e hlokometše dipego tša moragorago tša Phanele ya mebušo ye mentši ka ga Phetogo ya Tlelaemete, ebile e sepelelana le batšeakarolo ka moka bao ba tsenyago letsogo go matsapa a ka mo nageng.

src: BILLS Marine Pollution (Prevention of Pollution from Ships) Amendment Bill of 2021.
tgt: Melaokakanywa Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa Tšhilafatšo ya Mawatle (Thibelo ya Tšhilafatšo ye e Bakwago ke Dikepe) wa 2021.

src: Cabinet approved the Marine Pollution (Prevention of Pollution from Ships) Amendment Bill of 2021 for submission to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa Tšhilafatšo ya Mawatle (Thibelo ya Tšhilafatšo ye e bakwago ke Dikepe) wa 2021 gore setšhaba se fe ditshwaotshwao ka ga ona.

src: The Amendment Bill seeks to amend the Marine Pollution (Prevention of Pollution from Ships) Act, 1986 (Act 2 of 1986) and align it to the revised International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL).
tgt: Molaokakanywaphetošwa wo o nyaka go fetoša Molao wa Tšhilafatšo ya Mawatle (Thibelo ya Tšhilafatšo ye e bakwago ke Dikepe), wa 1986 (Molao wa bo 2 wa 1986) gomme o dira gore o sepelelane le Kwano ye e bušeleditšwego ya Boditšhabatšhab ka ga Thibelo ya Tšhilafatšo ye e bakwago ke Dikepe (MARPOL).

src: South Africa is a signatory to MARPOL, the main international convention covering prevention of pollution of the marine environment by ships from operational or accidental causes.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ke mosaenedi wa kwano ya MARPOL, e lego kwanokgolo ya boditšhabatšhaba yeo e akaretšago thibelo ya tšhilafatšo ya tikologo ya mawatle ka dikepe ka ge di sepetšwa fao goba ka lebaka la dikotsi.

src: The Amendment Bill will contribute towards the preservation of the marine environment by eliminating pollution of the sea by ships dispensing oil and harmful substances.
tgt: Molaokakanywaphetošwa wo o tla tsenya letsogo go lota tikologo ya mawatleng ka go fediša tšhilafatšo ya mawatle ka dikepe tšeo di tšhollago oli le dilo tše kotsi.

src: It also proposes that ships should use fuel with no more than 0,50% sulphur content or use approved fuel treatment systems.
tgt: O šišinya gape gore dikepe di swanetše go šomiša makhura ao a nago le salfiri ya go se fete 0,50% goba di šomiše ditshepedišo tše di dumeletšwego tša go hlwekiša makhura a tšona.

src: Companies Amendment Bill of 2021.
tgt: Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa Dikhamphani wa 2021.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Companies Amendment Bill of 2021 for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go phatlalatšwa ga Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa Dikhamphani wa 2021 gore setšhaba se fe ditshwaotshwao ka ga ona.

src: The Bill amends the Companies Act, 2008 (Act 71 of 2008).
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o fetoša Molao wa Dikhamphani wa 2008 (Molao wa bo 71 wa 2008).

src: Cabinet approved the current Bill for public consultation in August 2018 and the outcome thereof led to the redrafting of the amendments.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše Molaokakanywa wo gore setšhaba se reišane ka ga ona ka Phato 2018 gomme dipoelo tša ditherišano tše di feleleditše ka gore go ngwalwe leswa diphetošo tšeo di dirilwego.

src: The revised amendments provide more clarity in a number of clauses of the Bill, which seeks to reduce regulatory regime on businesses tighten anti-money laundering gaps strengthen the disclosure requirements and enhance the shareholder powers in a company.
tgt: Diphetošo tše di bušeleditšwego di fana ka tlhathollo ye e tseneletšego mabapi le ditemana tše mmalwa tša Molaokakanywa wo, tšeo di nyakago go fokotša seemo sa taolo go dikgwebo go maatlafatša masolo a go lwantšha le go hlwekiša tšhelete ye e hweditšwego ka bomenetša go maatlafatša ditumelelano mabapi le go tsebagatša le go maatlafatša maatla a bengdišere ka khamphaning.

src: National Climate Change Bill Cabinet approved the submission of the National Climate Change Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wa Bosetšhaba ka ga Phetogo ya Tlelaemete Kabinete e dumeletše go romelwa ga Molaokakanywa wa Bosetšhaba ka ga Phetogo ya Tlelaemete Palamenteng.

src: The Bill seeks to provide a legal instrument towards the implementation of the National Climate Change Response Policy.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o nyaka go fana ka setlabelo sa semolao mabapi le go phethagatša Melawana ya Bosetšhaba ya go Arabela Phetogo ya Tlelaemete.

src: It allows for the alignment of policies that will influence the country’s climate change response.
tgt: E dumelela gore melawana e beakanywe ka leswa yeo e tlago huetša go arabela ga naga ye mabapi le phetogo ya tlelaemete.

src: It also provides for the transitional arrangement for the country to move towards a lower carbon and climate-resilient economy.
tgt: E hlagiša gape gore go be le peakanyo ya diphetogo gore naga ye e kgone go fihlelela ekonomi yeo go yona go nago le meši ye mennyane le yeo e kgotlelelago tlelaemete.

src: The Bill has already gone through an extensive public consultation process involving relevant stakeholders.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o šetše o sepedišitšwe ka ditherišano tše di tseneletšego le setšhaba fao go bego go akaretšwa le batšeakarolo ba maleba.

src: APPOINTMENTSAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Bao ba Thwetšwego Mešomong Batho ka moka bao ba thwetšwego mešomong mangwalo a bona a dithuto a tla tiišetšwa le go netefaletšwa ka maleba.

src: Mr Smunda Mokoena as Chairperson of the National Energy Regulator of South Africa.
tgt: Morena Smunda Mokoena bjalo ka modulasetulo wa Bolaodi bja Bosetšhaba bja Enetši bja Afrika Borwa.

src: Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) vaccine roll-out Cabinet is encouraged by the millions of people in South Africa who have chosen to vaccinate against COVID-19, with over 17 million vaccine doses administered to date.
tgt: Lesolo la Meento ya Bolwetši bja Coronavirus (COVID-19) Kabinete e filwe hlohleletšo ke dimilione tša batho ba Afrika Borwa bao ba tšeerego sephetho sa go hlaba meento kgahlanong le COVID-19.

src: Cabinet thanked the religious formations, as well as the sports and arts fraternity, for embarking on vaccination campaigns to encourage the uptake of vaccines.
tgt: Kabinete e leboga dihlopha tša sedumedi, gotee le lefapha la dipapadi le bokgabo ka go tsenela masolo a meento go hlohleletša batho go hlaba meento.

src: The more people get vaccinated, the sooner the country will relax the current Adjusted Alert Level 2 restrictions.
tgt: Ge batho ka bontši ba hlaba meento, gona go ra gore naga ye e tla theošetša fase maemo a bjale a dikiletšo tša Maemotemošo a Bobedi.

src: This will inevitably result in the full opening of the economy to be able to grow and create much-needed jobs.
tgt: Se se tla dira gore ntle le pelaelo ditiragalo tša ikonomi di bulwe ka botlalo gore re kgone go godiša le go hloma mešomo yeo e nyakegago kudu.

src: Cabinet reiterates the call that to reduce new infections, we all have to continue wearing a mask in public, washing hands with soap and water or using a 70% alcohol-based sanitiser, and maintaining a safe social distance continues to reinforce the country’s approach in reducing new infections.
tgt: Kabinete e santše e gatelela kgoeletšo ye rego gore re fokotše diphetelo tše difsa tša bolwetši, re swanetše gore ka moka ga rena re tšwele pele go apara dimaseke ge re le gare ga batho le go šomiša meetse le sesepe goba sanithaesa sa alekhohole ya go feta 70%, le go tšwelapele go šielana sekgala go phethagatša morero wa naga ye wa go fokotša diphetelo tše difsa.

src: Vooma Vaccination Weekend campaign from 1 to 2 October 2021.
tgt: Lesolo la Vooma Vaccination Weekend go Thoma ka 1 go Fihla ka la 2 Diphalane 2021.

src: Cabinet urges unvaccinated South Africans and people living in South Africa to take advantage of the Vooma Vaccination Weekend which will take place around the country on Friday, 1 and Saturday, 2 October 2021.
tgt: Kabinete e dira boipiletšo go MaAfrika Borwa bao ba sa hlabago meento le batho bao ba dulago ka mo Afrika Borwa go šomiša monyetla wa Vooma Vaccination Weekend gore o ba hole.

src: The Vooma Vaccination Campaign Weekend is an inclusive national campaign supported by all social partners, including faith-based formations, traditional leaders, organised labour and business.
tgt: Lesolo la Vooma Vaccination Weekend ke lesolo la go akaretša batho ka moka la bosetšhaba leo le thekgwago ke badirišani ka moka setšhabeng, go akaretšwa le dihlopha tša sedumedi, baetapele ba setšo, bašomi bao ba ipopilego dihlopha le dikgwebo.

src: The target for this weekend is to vaccinate at least half a million people.
tgt: Go lebeletšwe gore gona mafelelo a beke ye, batho ba go feta 500 000 ba hlabe meento.

src: This is an opportunity for all adults to be vaccinated free of charge and without appointments at public, private and pop-up vaccination sites.
tgt: Wo ke monyetla go batho ba bagolo ka moka go hlaba meento ntle le tefo le ka ntle le go beakanya diketelo mafelong a go hlaba meento a mmušo, a praebete le fao batho ba ikelago ka bobona.

src: You don’t need to have health insurance or medical aid to receive the vaccine.
tgt: Ga go hlokege gore o be le inšorense ya maphelo goba medical aid gore o hlabe moento.

src: Leadership of government, business, labour and community formations will actively mobilise communities in all parts of the country to roll up their sleeves for the protection that comes with being vaccinated.
tgt: Baetapele ba mmušo, ba dikgwebo, ba bašomi le ba dihlopha tša batho setšhabeng ba tla rapa setšhaba ka mafolofolo dikarolong ka moka tša naga gore ba itokišetše tšhireletšo ye tlago le go hlaba moento.

src: Vooma Vaccination Weekend can help us achieve victory over the virus that has haunted us for more than a year.
tgt: Vooma Vaccination Weekend e ka re thuša go fenya baerase ye e re hlomerego lebaka la go feta ngwaga.

src: No-one should miss out on this opportunity.
tgt: Ga gona motho yo a swanetšego go fetwa ke monyetla wo.

src: Let’s all Stay Safe.
tgt: A re Bolokegeng ka Moka ga Rena.

src: Presidential Visit to Msikaba Bridge.
tgt: Ketelo ya Mopresidente Leporogong la Msikaba.

src: President Cyril Ramaphosa went to assess the development of infrastructure at the Msikaba Bridge at Lusikisiki in the Eastern Cape on Thursday, 23 September 2021.
tgt: Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tšwa go fetleka kgatelopele ya mošomo tlhabollong ya mananeokgoparara kua Leporogong la Msikaba, Lusikisiki go la Kapa Bohlabela ka Labone, 23 Lewedi 2021.

src: This R1,65 billion infrastructure project forms part of the N2 Wild Coast Road project.
tgt: Protšeke ye ya mananeokgoparara a go bitša R1,65 bilione e bopa karolo ya protšeke ya N2 Tseleng ya Wild Coast.

src: Apart from facilitating the convenient movement of people by connecting rural communities to urban centres around the country, the bridge will also stimulate investment and growth.
tgt: Ntle le go kgontšha gabonolo leemaema la batho ka go kgokaganya batho ba go dula dinagamagaeng le mafelo a metsesetoropo, leporogo le le tla hlohleletša dipeeletšo le kgolo ya ikonomi.

src: The N2 Wild Coast road network is one of government’s key Strategic Integrated Projects to catalyse economic growth at a national, provincial and local level.
tgt: Tsela ye ya go raragana ya N2 Wild Coast ke ye nngwe ya Diprotšeke tše kgolokgolo tša mmušo tša Mohlakanelwa le tše Logetšwego Maano go akgofiša go gola ga ikonomi maemong a bosetšhaba, a profense le lona felo leo.

src: Cabinet was pleased with the progress in its infrastructure investment drive, which remains a central pillar of the Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan (ERRP), with 88 projects worth more than R.3 trillion in the pipeline.
tgt: Kabinete e thabišitšwe ke kgatelopele ya mošomo lesolong la yona la dipeeletšo tša mananeokgoparara, e lego boikokotlelo bjo bohlokwa bja Leano la Tsošološo ya Ikonomi le go Boetšwa Sekeng ga yona (ERRP), ka diprotšeke tše 88 tša go bitša tšhelete ya go feta R.3 trilione tšeo di sa tlago.

src: International relations, trade and tourism.
tgt: Dikamano tša Boditšhabatšhaba, Bogwebi le tša Boeti.

src: Cabinet welcomed the decision by Germany to remove South Africa from its list of high-risk travel areas and plans by the United States of America to admit fully vaccinated travelers into the country.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše sephetho sa Germany sa go tloša Afrika Borwa lenaneong la yona la mafelo a goba le kotsi ye kgolo ge a etelwa le dithulaganyo tša Amerika tša go amogela baeti bao ba entilwego ka botlalo ka nageng yeo.

src: Cabinet however expressed disappointment at the United Kingdom’s (UK) decision to keep South Africa on its travel red list of countries.
tgt: Le ge go le bjalo, Kabinete e laeditše ka fao e nyamišitšwego ke sephetho sa United Kingdom (UK) sa go tlogela Afrika Borwa lenaneong la naga yeo la dinaga tše lego kotsing ye kgolo go ka etelwa.

src: There is no reasonable basis for keeping South Africa on the list given our progress in combating the COVID-19 pandemic and rapidly declining infection rate and our intensive vaccination programme.
tgt: Ga gona mabaka a go kwagala a go tlogela Afrika Borwa lenaneong leo kudu ka ge re fihleletše tše ntši go lwantšha leuba la COVID-19 le go fokotša ka pela palo ye diphetelo tša malwetši gotee le lenaneo la rena la motlalanaga la go hlaba meento.

src: Cabinet was also briefed by the Department of International Relations and Cooperation on progress made to have South Africa removed from the red list.
tgt: Kabinete e sedimošitšwe ke Kgoro ya Dikamano tša Boditšhabatšhaba le Tirišano ya Makala ka kgatelopele ye fihleletšwego go tloša Afrika Borwa lenaneong la dinaga tše lego kotsing ya bolwetši.

src: Cabinet is optimistic that the UK Government will revisit its unfavourable decision, which is not only affecting the tourism industry but businesses from both countries, families and other sectors of the economy.
tgt: Kabinete e nale tshepho ya gore Mmušo wa UK o tla boela wa lebeledišiša sephetho sa ona se lego kgahlanong le naga ye, seo se sa amego fela intasteri ya boeti eupša se amago gampe dikgwebo go tšwa dinageng tše ka bobedi, malapa le mafapha a mangwe a ikonomi.

src: Economic recovery Cabinet welcomed the launch of the Business Loss Registration Portal to register businesses affected by the unrest that took place between 9 and 19 July 2021 in KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng and other affected areas.
tgt: Go Boetšwa Sekeng ga Ikonomi Kabinete e amogetše go tsebagatšwa ga Phothale ya Boingwadišo bja Tahlegelo ya Kgwebo go ngwadiša dikgwebo tšeo di amilwego ke megwanto yeo e diragetšego magareng ga la 9 le la 19 Mosegamanye gola KwaZulu-Natal, Gauteng le mafelong a mangwe ao a amilwego ke megwanto ye.

src: The registration portal collects data from affected businesses to better coordinate relief measures and to inform future interventions.
tgt: Phothale ye ya boingwadišo e hwetša tshedimošo go tšwa dikgwebong tšeo di amilwego ke megwanto go beakanya bokaone magato a kimollo le go tla ka magato a go rarolla se ao a tlo dirišwago kamoso.

src: It serves as a single governmental entry point for businesses to indicate the extent of their losses.
tgt: Phothale ye ke mokgwa o le noši wa mmušo wo ka ona dikgwebo di ka laetšago ka fao di lobilego ka gona.

src: Cabinet called on all affected business owners to register on the portal at WEBTOKEAlternatively, they may call 080 006 0085.0 for assistance between 08:00 and 17:00 on weekdays.
tgt: Kabinete e dirile boipiletšo go bengdikgwebo ka moka bao ba amilwego ke megwanto go ingwadiša phothaleng ye mo go WEBTOKEKa go le le ngwe, ba ka letšetša 080 006 0085.0 go hwetša thušo magareng ga 08:00 le 17:00 gare ga beke.

src: Through the Department of Small Business Development, a total of 192 applications from small to medium business owners that were affected by the unrest had been received.
tgt: Ka Kgoro ya Tlhabollo ya Dikgwebopotlana, palomoka ya dikgopelo tše 192 go tšwa go bengdikgwebo tše nnyane le tša magareng bao ba amilwego ke mogwanto wo di amogetšwe.

src: Cabinet is pleased that a total of R54,2 million has been approved to be allocated to these business owners.
tgt: Kabinete e thabišitšwe ke gore palomoka ya go lekana R54,2 milione e dumeletšwe gore e abelwe bona bengdikgwebo ba.

src: Resumption of South African Airways (SAA) flights.
tgt: Go Tšwetšwapele ga Difofane tša Tirelo ya Difofane ya Afrika Borwa (SAA) Kabinete e amogela go tšwetšwapele ga difofane ka SAA, fao go šomago fela maeto a se makae magareng ga Johannesburg le Motsekapa.

src: Cabinet welcomed the recent resumption of flights by the SAA, which operates a few routes between Johannesburg and Cape Town.
tgt: Khamphani ye ya difofane ya bosetšhaba e tla fofiša batho goya metsemešate ya dinaga tša Afrika go swana le Accra (Ghana), Kinshasa (Democratic Republic of the Congo), Harare (Zimbabwe), Lusaka (Zambia) le Maputo (Mozambique), ebile mafelo a mangwe a mantši a tlo lokelwa ge maemo a mebaraka a kaonafala.

src: The national carrier will also fly to African capitals such as Accra (Ghana), Kinshasa (Democratic Republic of the Congo), Harare (Zimbabwe), Lusaka (Zambia) and Maputo (Mozambique), and more destinations will be added to the routes as market conditions improve.
tgt: Kabinete e dirile boipiletšo go MaAfrika Borwa ka moka go thekga SAA yeo e beakantšwego ka lefsa, e bago seo se laetšago mathomomayo a paka ye mpsha diphofong tša Afrika Borwa.

src: Cabinet called on all South Africans to support the restructured SAA, which marks the beginning of a new era in South African aviation.
tgt: Yuniti ya Maitshwaro a Maleba a Tshepedišo ya Makala a Mmušo, Bobotegi le Thušo ya Sethekniki go tša Kgalemo (PA-EID-TAU).

src: Cabinet welcomed the launch of the PA-EID-TAU, which will strengthen government’s efforts in the fight against corruption in the Public Service.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše go tsebagatšwa ga PA-EID-TAU, e bago yuniti yeo e tiišeletšago matsapa a mmušo twantšhong ya kgahlanong le bosenyi Ditirelong tša Mmušo.

src: The PA-EID-TAU will oversee the implementation of public service ethics and anti-corruption policies such as conducting business with the State, performance of other remunerative work, discipline management and implementation of lifestyle audits.
tgt: PA-EID-TAU e tla bea leihlo go phethagatšwa ga maitshwaro a maleba ditirelong tša mmušo le dipholisi tše kgahlanong le bosenyi go swana le go dira kgwebo le Mmušo, go diragatšwa ga mešomo e mengwe ya go tsentšha meputso, taolo ya kgalemo le go phethagatšwa ga dipego tša bohlakiši tša ka fao batho ba phelago ka gona.

src: Cabinet called on public officials to remain resolute in stamping out corruption.
tgt: Kabinete e dira boipiletšo go bašomedi ba mmušo go ema ka molomo wa lehlabula mo matsapeng a bona a go fediša bosenyi.

src: By simply taking the lead in reporting all corruption-related activities taking place in government institutions, we can ensure a better tomorrow and leave a lasting legacy for future generations.
tgt: Ka go no ba batho bao ba eteletšego pele ka go bega ditiragalo ka moka tša go amana le bosenyi bjo bo diragalagong Makaleng le ditheong tša mmušo, re ka kgona go ihlolela bokamoso bjo kaone le go tlogelela bao ba tlago ka morago ga rena bohwa bja goyagoile.

src: 2021 Local Government Elections (LGE).
tgt: Dikgetho tša 2021 tša Pušo Selegae (LGE).

src: Cabinet commends the 1,7 million first-time voters who registered during the voter registration weekend of 18 and 19 September.
tgt: Kabinete e retile bakgethi bao ba tla bego ba kgetha lekga la mathomo ba 1,7 milione bao ba ngwadišitšego ka beke ya go ingwadišetša go kgetha ka la 18 le 19 Lewedi.

src: This was young people’s way of saying they want to play their part in our democracy by electing local leadership.
tgt: Go ingwadišetša go kgetha ke mokgwa wo baswa ba laetšago gore ba nyaka go kgatha tema ka gare ga temokrasi ya rena ka go kgetha baetapele mafelong ao ba tšwago go ona.

src: As young people constitute the majority of our population, the enthusiasm of young people to be part of our electoral processes is something we welcome and respect.
tgt: Ka ge baswa ba bopa palo ye kgolo ya setšhaba sa gaborena, Lethabo la baswa go ba karolo ya ditshepedišo tša rena tša dikgetho ke taba yeo re amogelago ka diatla tše pedi le go e hlompha.

src: The 2021 LGE scheduled to take place on 1 November 2021 provides South Africans with the opportunity to exercise their constitutional right to elect their public representatives.
tgt: Dikgetho tša Pušoselegae (LGE) tša 2021 tšeo di rulaganyeditšwego go swarwa ka la 1 Dibatsela 2021 di fa MaAfrika Borwa monyetla wa go phethagatša ditokelo tša bona tša molaotheo go kgetha baetapele ba bona setšhabeng.

src: Voters who are not able to cast their votes on Election Day and those who are not able to travel to voting stations due to physical infirmity or disability can vote by Special Vote on the two days preceding Election Day.
tgt: Bakgethi bao ba sa kgoneng go kgetha ka Letšatši la Dikgetho le bao ba sa kgoneng go fihla diteišeneng tša go kgetha ka baka la malwetši mebeleng goba bogole ba ka kgetha ka Diboutu tša Moswananoši matšatši a mabedi pele ga Letšatši la Dikgetho.

src: Applications for special votes opened on 20 September 2021 and will close on 4 October 2021 at 17:00.
tgt: Dikgopelo tša diboutu tša moswananoši di tla bulwa ka la 20 Lewedi 2021 tša buša tša tswalelwa ka la 4 Diphalane 2021 ka iri ya bohlano mathapama.

src: Gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).
tgt: Dikgaruru tša go Ikala ka Bong le Polao ya Basadi (GBVF).

src: Cabinet welcomed the double life sentence handed down to Mr Sbusiso Nkosi (36) by the Mpumalanga Division of the High Court on Monday, 13 September 2021, for the rape and murder of Ms Nomcebo Simelane (23) on 5 September 2020.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše kahlolelo tše pedi tša bophelo ka moka tšeo di ahloletšwego Morena Sbusiso Nkosi (36) ka Kgorotsheko ya Godimo ya Lekala la Mpumalanga, ka la 13 Lewedi 2021, ka go kata le go bolaya Mohumagatšana Nomcebo Simelane (23) ka la 5 Lewedi 2020.

src: The court sentenced the rapist and murderer to two life imprisonment terms and an additional three years’ imprisonment for theft, which will run concurrently.
tgt: Kgorotsheko e ahloletše sekata se le mmolai dikwebo tše pedi tša bophelo ka moka le sekwebo sa tlaleletšo sa go golegwa mengwaga ye meraro ka baka la bohodu, gomme dikwebo tše di a latelana.

src: This is a firm warning to all perpetrators of GBVF that they will be arrested and face the full might of the law.
tgt: Ye ke temošo ye tiišeleditšwego letsogo go batho ka moka ba go dira bosenyi bja GBVF gore ba tla golegwa le go lebana le letsogo la molao ka botlalo.

src: By working together with the police and law-enforcement agencies, we can make our streets and communities safer for all.
tgt: Ka go šomišana le maphodisa le mabotho a phethagatšo ya molao, re ka dira gore mekgotha ya rena ka mo nageng le batho setšhabeng ba bolokege ka moka ga bona.

src: Report all GBVF-related incidents to the police or call the National GBVF Command Centre: 0800 428 428 or STOP Gender Violence Helpline: 0800 150 150 / *120*7867#9.
tgt: Bega ditiragalo ka moka tša go amana le GBVF maphodiseng goba o letšetše Senthara ya Bosetšhaba ya GBVF mo go: 0800 428 428 goba Mogala wa PHEDIŠO ya Dikgaruru tša Bong mo go: 0800 150 150 / *120*7867#10.

src: Registration of customary marriages.
tgt: Boingwadišo bja Manyalo a Setšo.

src: Cabinet noted the High Court, KwaZulu-Natal Division judgment in the matter involving the applicant, Ms Phumza Ethel Mankayi and the respondents, the Minister of Home Affairs, Ms Ntombizakhe Portia Miya and the Master of the High Court of South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile kahlolo ya Kgorotsheko ya Godimo ya Lekala la KwaZulu-Natal tabeng ya go amana le modirakgopelo, Mohumagadi Phumza Ethel Mankayi le baarabedi tabeng ye, Tona ya Merero ya Selegae, Mohumagadi Ntombizakhe Portia Miya le Kantorokgolo ya Kgorotsheko ya Godimo ya Afrika Borwa.

src: The judgment affirms the rights of people married under the Recognition of Customary Marriages Act, 1998 (Act 120 of 1998).
tgt: Kahlolo ye e kgonthišiša ditokelo tša batho bao ba nyetšwego ka fase ga Molao wa Temogo ya Manyalo a Setšo, 1998 (Molao 120 wa 1998).

src: Cabinet calls on couples to register their customary marriages at Home Affairs within three months of their marriage.
tgt: Kabinete e dira boipiletšo go banyalani bao ba nyalanego ka setšo go yo ngwadiša manyalo a bona a setšo Kgorong ya Merero ya Selegae mo nakong ya dikgwedi tše tharo morago ga ge ba nyalane.

src: The Minister of Home Affairs has extended the registration period to 30 June 2024.
tgt: Tona ya Merero ya Selegae e okeditše nako ya go ngwadiša manyalo ao a setšo go fihla ka la 30 Phupu 2024.

src: This is to cater for those whose marriages that were not registered within three months.
tgt: Se se diretšwe go akaretša bao manyalo a bona a sa kago a ngwadišwa mo dikgweding tše tharo tša go nyala ga bona.

src: To register, people need to bring proof of lobola negotiations or a letter and an affidavit from people getting married and their witnesses, indicating that a marriage was entered into or celebrated.
tgt: Go ingwadiša, batho ba swanetše go tliša bohlatse bja ditherišano tša magadi goba lengwalo le afitabiti go tšwa go bao ba nyalanago le dihlatse tša bona, tšeo di laetšago gore lenyalo le bile gona goba le ketekilwe.

src: To date, only 99 491 customary marriages have been registered at Home Affairs since the law came into effect in November 2000.Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Go fihla lehono, ke fela manyalo a setšo a 99 491 ao a ngwadišitšwego Kgorong ya Merero ya Selegae ga e sale go tloga mola molao o thomang go tsenywa tirišong ka Dibatsela 2000.Diphetho tša Kabinete.

src: South Africa Investment Conference (SAIC).
tgt: Khonferense ya Afrika Borwa ya Dipeeletšo (SAIC).

src: Cabinet approved the scheduling of the next SAIC to take place in March 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše dithulaganyo tša go beakanya SAIC ye tlago yeo e tlo swarwago ka Hlakola 2022.

src: The conference is on its third year and aims to attract R1,2 trillion investments over five years.
tgt: Khonferense ye e mo ngwageng wa yona wa boraro ebile nepokgolo ya yona ke go goketša dipeeletšo tša go bitša R1,2 trilione mo mengwageng ye mehlano.

src: The investment drive continues to build on the two previous successful SAICs.
tgt: Lesolo la dipeeletšo le tšwelapele go tlaleletša dikopano tša SAIC tše pedi tša go feta tšeo di atlegilego.

src: The details of the conference and date will be announced at a later stage.
tgt: Tshedimošo ka botlalo ya khonferense ye le letšatšikgwedi leo e tlo swarwago ka lona di tla tsebagatšwa ka moragonyana.

src: Broadcasting Digital Migration (BDM) programme Cabinet was apprised on the country’s BDM programme.
tgt: Lenaneo la go Fetogela Kgašong ya Titšithale (BDM).

src: Substantial progress has been made in migrating some parts of the country from analogue to digital platforms.
tgt: Kabinete e hlalošeditšwe ka lenaneo la naga ye la BDKgatelopele ye e wišago pelo e fihleletšwe go huduša dikarolo tše dingwe tša naga ye go tloga dikgašong tša megala goya go tša titšithale.

src: Cabinet approved the revised integrated analogue switch-off implementation plan, which is a schedule to complete the remaining areas by March 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše leanophethagatšo leo le fetlekilwego la mohlakanelwa la go fetošetša megala goya go ditšithale, e lego šetulu yeo e beakanyeditšwego go phethagatša ka botlalo mafelo ao a šaletšego morago pele ga Manthole 2022.

src: South Africa is one of many countries in the world that have committed to expedite the digital migration project, which will lead to a complete analogue switch-off in 2022.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ke ye nngwe ya dinaga tše ntši mo lefaseng tšeo di ikgafetšego go phethagatša ka bonako protšeke ya go hudugela theknolotšing ya titšithale, yeo pheletšo ya yona e tla bago gore kgašo ya megala e tla tšeelwa legato ke ya titšithale ka 2022.

src: Cabinet endorsed the collaborative approach adopted towards fast-tracking the finalisation of the migration of the whole country from analogue to digital platforms.
tgt: Kabinete e thekgile lemanoga la mohlakanelwa leo le dirišwago go lebeletšwe go akgofiša go rungwa ga go hudugela ga naga ka moka go tloga kgašong ya megala go ya kgašong ya titšithale.

src: National Policy on the Prevention and Management of Learner Pregnancy in Schools Cabinet approved the National Policy on the Prevention and Management of Learner Pregnancy in Schools.
tgt: Pholisi ya Bosetšhaba ya Thibelo le Taolo ya go Ima ga Barutwana Dikolong Kabinete e dumeletše Pholisi ya Bosetšhaba ya Thibelo le Taolo ya go Ima ga Barutwana Dikolong.

src: The policy responds to the 2012 Court Judgement that ruled against the Department of Basic Education on certain clauses that called for learners to take leave of absence from school for up to two years post-delivery.
tgt: Pholisi ye e arabela Kahlolelo ya Kgorotsheko ya 2012 yeo e tšeerego sephetho sa kgahlanong le Kgoro ya Thuto ya Motheo mo ditemaneng tše itšego tšeo di bego di dira gore barutwana ba lofišwe go tla dikolong lebaka la mengwaga ye mebedi morago ga go belega.

src: The policy provides for an enabling environment to support learners and prevent discrimination against pregnant learners.
tgt: Pholisi ye e fana ka tikologo ya go kgontšha go thekga barutwana le go efoga kgethollo kgahlanong le barutwana bao ba imilego.

src: It also provides for access to comprehensive pregnancy prevention information counselling and care guidelines, as well as the setting up of policy management and coordinating structures.
tgt: Pholisi ye e fana gape ka khumanego ya tshedimošo ye feletšego ka botlalo ya thibelo ya go ima ditlhahlo tša thobamaikutlo le tša tlhokomelo, gotee le go hloma ditheo tša taolo ya pholisi le tša peakanyo.

src: The policy has gone through extensive consultation with all relevant stakeholders and is aligned with all relevant laws.
tgt: Pholisi ye e šetše e fetile ditherišanong tša motlalanaga ebile e gata ka mošito o tee le melao ka moka ye maleba.

src: Accession to the 2003 United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Convention for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH).
tgt: Kwanelo go Kopano ya 2003 ya Ditšhabakopano ya Setheo sa tša Thuto, tša Saenthefiki le tša Setšo (UNESCO) go Šireletša Bohwa bja Setšo bjo Lego Dikgopolong (ICH).

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s accession to the 2003 UNESCO Convention for the Safeguarding of ICThe convention provides for the safeguarding, preservation and promotion of ICH by the respective member states.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše kwanelo ya Afrika Borwa Kopanong ya 2003 ya UNESCO go Šireletša ICKopano ye e fana ka monyetla wa go šireletšwa, go lotwa le go hlohleletšwa ga ICH ka mebušo ya go fapafapana ya dinaga tšeo e lego maloko.

src: The ICH includes amongst others community cultural spaces, knowledge, objects and artefacts in communities.
tgt: ICH e akaretša gare ga tše dingwe ditšo tše lego setšhabeng, tsebo, didirišwa le dibetlwa mo setšhabeng.

src: The convention obliges member states to identify, define and devise appropriate measures for their preservation.
tgt: Kopano ye e gapeletša mebušo yeo e lego maloko go hlaola, go hlaloša le go hlama magato a maleba go lota bohwa bjo.

src: It also encourages countries to adopt legal, technical administrative and financial measures to safeguard and promote ICThe accession will be tabled to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: E hlohleletša gape le dinaga go diriša magato a semolao, a tsamaišo ya sethekniki le a go amana le tša ditšhelete go šireletša le go hlohleletša ICKwanelo ye e tlo hlagišetšwa Palamente gore e dumelelwe.

src: UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC).
tgt: Kopano ya Ditšhabakopano Kgahlanong le Bosenyi (UNCAC).

src: Cabinet approved the publication of South Africa’s Review Report on the implementation of the Convention.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše phatlalatšo ya Pego ya Afrika Borwa ya tshekatsheko ka phethagatšo ya Kopano.

src: South Africa ratified the UNCAC in 2004.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e dumeletše UNCAC ka 2004.

src: Member states are peer reviewed on the implementation of the convention.
tgt: Mebušo yeo e lego maloko a kopano ye e sekasekwa goya ka phethagatšo ya kopano ye.

src: South Africa was first reviewed in 2012 on the implementation of the criminalisation and law-enforcement interventions, and also on its international cooperation adherence.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e sekasekilwe la mathomo ka 2012 ka phethagatšo ya magato a bosenyi le a phethagatšo ya molao, le gape ka fao e latelago tshepedišo ka gona tšhomišanong ya boditšhabatšhaba.

src: The current 2019/20 review report focused on preventative and asset recovery measures.
tgt: Pego ya phetleko ya bjale ya 2019/20 e šeditše magato a thibelo le go hwetšwa ga dithoto.

src: The review mechanism promotes constructive collaboration by, amongst others, providing technical assistance programmes to the member states.
tgt: Magato a a phetleko a hlohleletša tirišano ye agišago ka, gare ga tše dingwe, go fana ka mananeo a thušo ya sethekniki mebušong yeo e lego maloko a kopano ye.

src: Postponement for South Africa to host the World Maritime Day Parallel Event (WMDPE).
tgt: Go Fegwa ga Afrika Borwa go Swara Letšatši la Lefase la Mabopo le Tiragalo ya go Lebana le Lona (WMDPE).

src: The International Maritime Organisation has once again granted South Africa permission to postpone the hosting of the WMDPE owing to COVID-19.
tgt: Mokgatlo wa Boditšhatšhaba wa Mabopo o file gape gape Afrika Borwa tumelelo ya go fega go swara WMDPE ka baka la COVID-19.

src: The postponement from October 2021 to October 2022, follows the first one in 2020 as a result of the pandemic.
tgt: Phego ye go tloga ka Diphalane 2021 go fihla ka Diphalane 2022 e latela ya mathomo ka 2020 ka baka la leuba la COVID-19.

src: Bills National Council on GBV and Femicide (GBVF) Bill of 2021 Cabinet approved the publication of the National Council on GBVF Bill of 2021 in the Government Gazette for public comment.
tgt: Melaokakanywa Khansele ya Bosetšhaba ka Molaokakanywa wa 2021 wa GBV le Polao ya Basadi (GBVF) Kabinete e dumeletše phatlalatšo ya Khansele ya Bosetšhaba ka Molaokakanywa wa 2021 wa GBVF ka gare ga Kuranta ya Mmušo gore setšhaba se fe ditshwayotshwayo.

src: The Bill responds to the strategic directive from the National Strategic Plan (NSP) on GBVF that was approved by Cabinet in March 2020.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o arabela tlhahlo ye logetšwego maano go Leanopeakanyo la Bosetšhaba (NSP) ka GBVF leo le dumeletšwego ke Kabinete ka Hlakola 2020.

src: The Bill proposes the establishment of a representative independent council to oversee the NSP on GBVNational Veld and Forest Fire Amendment (NVFFA) Bill of 2021 Cabinet approved the submission of the National Veld and Forest Fire Amendment Bill of 2021 to Parliament.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o šišinya go hlongwa ga khansele ya boetapele ye ikemego go bea leihlo NSP godimo ga GBVMolaokakanywaphetošwa wa Bosetšhaba wa 2021 wa Mello ya Tlhaga (NVFFA) Kabinete e dumeletše tlhagišo Palamenteng ya Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa Bosetšhaba wa 2021 wa Mello ya Tlhaga.

src: This Bill was first submitted to Parliament in 2017 and was sent back for further consultation with the public.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o hlagišeditšwe Palamente la Mathomo ka 2017 ebile o bušeditšwe morago gore setšhaba se fe ditshwayotshwayo tša sona ka ona.

src: Among other provisions, the Bill establishes structures in the public sector and at community level that will work together to mitigate veldfire risks, and promote effective compliance and law enforcement.
tgt: Godimo ga dipeakanyetšo tše dingwe, Molaokakanywa wo o o hloma ditheo lefapheng la mmušo le maemong a setšhaba tšeo di tla šomago mmogo go fediša kotsi ya mello ya tlhaga le go hlohleletša kobamelo ye nago le mohola le phethagatšo ya molao.

src: Uncontrolled veldfires are responsible for environmental degradation, loss of jobs, displacement of communities, and general destruction of infrastructure, livestock, habitat and biodiversity.
tgt: Mello ya tlhaga ya go se laolege ke yona e hlolago go gwahlafala ga tikologo, tobo ya mešomo, go hudušwa ga batho setšhabeng, le tshenyo ka kakaretšo ya mananeokgoparara, diruiwa, madulo a tšona le diphedi tša go fapafapana.

src: UPCOMING EVENTSustainable Infrastructure Development Symposium South Africa (SIDSSA).
tgt: Kopano Tlhabollo ya Mananeokgoparara a go Swarelela ya Afrika Borwa (SIDSSA).

src: Government will be hosting the SIDSSA 2021 on Wednesday, 6 and Thursday, 7 October 2021.
tgt: Mmušo o tla swara SIDSSA ya 2021 ka Laboraro, 6 le ka Labone 7 Diphalane 2021.

src: The symposium will engage with a range of stakeholders to revitalise the infrastructure pipeline.
tgt: Kopanong ye go tla boledišanwa le bakgathatema ba go fapafapana go tsošološa mananeokgoparara ao a tlogo dirwa.

src: The SIDSSA infrastructure pipeline aims to contribute to industrialisation and job creation as envisaged in the ERRP and the Re-imagined Industrial Strategy.
tgt: Mananeokgoparara a SIDSSA ao a tlogo dirwa a nepile go kgatha tema go hloma diintasteri le go hloma mešomo go ya ka fao go boletšwego ka gare ga ERRP le Leano la Diintasteri leo le Naganišitšwego ka leswa.

src: The interventions identified aim to boost demand and ensure effective coordination of all infrastructure players.
tgt: Magato a go rarolla seemo se ao a hlaotšwego a nepile go rotoša nyakego le go netefatša tsamaišo ye nago le mohola ya bakgathatema ka moka ba mananeokgoparara.

src: It is envisaged that these interventions will also contribute to building a resilient economy by accelerating infrastructure delivery.
tgt: Go ukangwa gore magato a go rarolla seemo se a tla thuša gape go bopa ikomomi yeo e tieletšego ka go akgofiša kabo ya mananeokgoparara.

src: The SIDSSA 2021 is held under the theme: “Quality infrastructure for development, recovery and inclusive growth”.
tgt: SIDSSA ya 2021 e tla swarwa ka fase ga morero wo: “Mananeokgoparara a hlwahlwa bakeng sa tlhabollo, poelosekeng le kgolo ya go akaretša batho ka moka”.

src: Transport Month 2021 October is dedicated to bringing a sharp focus to transport issues in the country.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Dinamelwa ya 2021 Diphalane ke kgwedi yeo e kgafetšwego go lebiša šedi ye kgolo mererong ya dinamelwa ka mo nageng.

src: This is the 16th year that the country observes Transport Month.
tgt: Wo ke ngwaga wa bo-16 mola naga e thomago go keteka Kgwedi ya Dinamelwa.

src: Cabinet approved this year’s theme: “Together, let’s fix transport”.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše morero wa ngwaga wo: “Mmogo, a re swarišaneng go lokiša dinamelwa”.

src: The campaign’s slogan is “Brika Bova: Riding the wave to a better transport system for tomorrow”.
tgt: Mmolelwana wa lesolo le ke “Brika Bova: A re phegeleleng peakanyo ye kaonafetšego ya dinamelwa go direla kamoso”.

src: The transport sector is an important socio-economic element in South Africa.
tgt: Lefapha la dinamelwa ke karolo ye bohlokwa ya ikonomi maphelong a batho ka mo Afrika Borwa.

src: This year the campaign will focus on positioning transport as a key enabler in the country’s economic recovery create an awareness and educate on the safety in all transport modes, and also showcase the improvements made in the transport system.
tgt: Ngwaga wo, lesolo le le tla setša go bea sekeng dinamelwa bjalo ka sekgontšhi se bohlokwa go boetša ikonomi ya naga ye sekeng go lemoša batho le go ba ruta ka polokego ya mehuta ka moka dinamelwa, le go laetša gape dikaonafatšo tšeo di dirilwego peakanyong ya dinamelwa.

src: The Department of Transport will share the month’s activities with the public and more information is available on www.
tgt: Kgoro ya Dinamelwa e tla abelana ditiragalo tša kgwedi ye le setšhaba ebile tshedimošo ka botlalo e ya hwetšagala mo go www.

src: transport.
tgt: transport.
