tgt: kopano ye ke karolo ya lesolo la mmušo la dipeeletšo leo le nepilego go goketša peeletšo ya tšhelete ya go lekana ditrilione tše tša diranta mo mengwageng e mehlano yeo e tlago, gomme kopano ye e goketša dikemedi go tšwa ka Afrika Borwa le lefaseng ka bophara go tlo boledišana ka menyetla ya go beeletša.

src: Since the first investment conference in 2018, South Africa has attracted R774 billion in commitments across a wide range of economic sectors.
tgt: Esale go tloga kopanong ya mathomo ya dipeeletšo ka 2018, Afrika Borwa e gokeditše dibilione tše 774 tša diranta tša dineelo ka Makaleng a go fapafapana a ikonomi.

src: As of February 2022, those firms who have completed their reporting, have advised that R314 billion (40,6%) of the committed investment pledges have been expended.
tgt: Kabinete e thabišitšwe ke gore ditšhwaana tša meento ya COVID-19 tšeo di batamelago dimilione tše 32 di šetše di hlabetšwe batho, le gore dipersente tše 42 tša batho ba bagolo di šetše di entetšwe ka botlalo.

src: Update on the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) Cabinet acknowledged the country’s efforts towards the fight against COVID-19 but cautioned that the battle is not yet over, and urged all people in South Africa to remain vigilant and continue protecting themselves to stop the spread of the deadly virus.
tgt: Le ge go le bjalo, batho bao ba sego ba entelwa ba sa tšwela pele go se šireletšege kgahlanong le COVID-19 gomme ba ipea kotsing le go bea bao ba lego kgauswi le bona kotsing.

src: Cabinet is pleased that almost 32 million COVID-19 vaccine doses have been administered and that over 42 percent of our adult population is fully vaccinated.
tgt: Go entelwa e sa dutše e le yona tsela e kaonekaone ya go lwa le COVID-19, gomme Kabinete e ipiletša go batho ka moka bao nago le mengwaga e 12 le go feta gore ba se sa senya nako, ba entelwe.

src: However, unvaccinated people still remain unprotected against COVID-19 and pose a health risk to themselves and those around them.
tgt: Meento ya go matlafatša bjale e gona bakeng sa batho ka bontšhi gomme Kabinete e ipiletša go bao ba nago le maswanedi gore ba e hlabelwe ka pela ka moo go kgonegago.

src: Vaccination remains the best way to fight COVID-19, and Cabinet calls on everyone aged 12 years and above to vaccinate without further delay.
tgt: Re swanetše gape re tšwele pele go apare dimaske tšeo di thibelago molomo le nko, re hlape diatla goba re tlole sanithaesa ka mehla, re bule sekgoba le go netefatša gore re bula matsikangope gore moya o tsene.

src: President Ramaphosa appointed Adv Andrea Johnson to head the NPA’s Investigating Directorate and Ambassador Thembisile Majola as the new Director-General (DG) of the SSThe President also appointed Adv Navilla Somaru as Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) in the Free State Adv Matodzi Rachel Makhari-Sekhaolelo as DPP in North West and Adv Nicolette Bell as DPP in the Western Cape.
tgt: Ketelo ya Peoleihlo ya Kabo ya Ditirelo Kabinete e amogetše ketelo yeo e atlegilego ya peoleihlo ka Tona ya Mešomo ya Setšhaba le Mananeokgoparara, Mme Patricia de Lille le Tona ka Kantorong ya Mopresidente, Morena Mondli Gungubele protšekeng ya mararankodi a tsela ya N2 ka Mmasepalengmogolo wa Nelson Mandela Bay ka Kapa Bohlabela ka Labobedi la 8 Hlakola 2022.

src: These appointments will strengthen our capacity to investigate and prosecute all acts of crime and corruption.
tgt: Ketelo ye ke karolo ya lesolo la mmušo la tekolo ya ka mehla ya tšwelopele yeo e dirilwego ge go etla phethagatšong ya Leano la Peeletšo ka Mananeokgoparara la go tsošološa ikonomi le go hlola mešomo.

src: The visit forms part of government’s initiative towards a more regular direct assessment of the progress made on the implementation of the Infrastructure Investment Plan to reignite the economy and create jobs.
tgt: Letšatši le ke monyetla wa go lebelela morago go bona leeto leo re le sepetšego ge go etla tšweletšongpele ya tekatekano ya bong le seo se hlokago go dirwa gore re be setšhaba seo se nago le tekatekano ya bong.

src: International Women’s Day South Africa joined the international community in commemorating International Women’s Day on Tuesday, 8 March 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše gape go kgethwa ga Afrika Borwa go ba Modulasetulo kopanong ya Komišene ya tša Maemo a Basadi ya Ditšhabakopano yeo e tlo swarwago go tloga ka Mošupologo wa la 14 Hlakola 2022 go fihla ka la 25 Hlakola 2022.

src: Cabinet also welcomed the appointment of South Africa to the Chairship of the sixty-sixth session of the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women to be held from Monday, 14 March to Friday, 25 March State security Cabinet noted the United States Treasury’s arrest of individuals allegedly involved in money laundering.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše go tsena ka bogare ka pela ga makala phethagatšo ya molao, elego seo se bušitšego khutšo ka lefelong leo, mmogo le go golegwa ga batho bao ba belaelwago go ba bona bahlodi ba dikgaruru sethabeng.

src: We continue to work with our international partners to stem the flow of illicit funds.
tgt: Ditšhaba di hloleletšwa go šomiša mekgwa wa khutšo go rarolla dithulano gape le go bega ditiragalo ka moka tšeo di sego molaong go makala a phethagatšo ya molao.

src: Cabinet welcomed the speedy intervention by law-enforcement agencies, which resulted in calm being restored in the area and the arrest of several alleged perpetrators of public violence.
tgt: Go Rekišwa Okšeneng ga Maphoto a Seyalemoya ao a Nyakwago Kudu Kabinete e lebogišitše ba Taolo ya Dikgokagano ya Afrika Borwa (ICASA) ge ba thomile go rekiša maphoto a seyalemoya ao a nyakwago kudu okšeneng le ge go na le melato yeo e tšwelago pele.

src: Communities are urged to use peaceful means to resolve disputes and to report all illegal activities to law-enforcement agencies.
tgt: Kabinete e lebogišitše gape batho bao ba nyakago go reka maphoto bao ba tšeerego karolo ka okšeneng ka Labobedi la 8 le Labone la 10 Hlakola 2022, elego seo se bontšhago maikemišetšo a intaseteri ya tša kgokagano go tšwela pele go beeletša ka mananeongkgoparara a ditšithale ka Afrika Borwa.

src: Economy.1 Cabinet has noted the gross domestic product (GDP) figures released by Statistics South Africa recently which showed that South Africa’s GDP grew by percent in the fourth quarter of 2021, after shrinking by percent in the third quarter of 2021.
tgt: Mmušo o tšwela pele o ikgafile go hlola sebaka seo se kgontšhago maphoto a seyalemoya gore a šomišwe ka botlalo, gomme a sa šomišwe feela ke didintaseteri tša kgokagano eupša le go hola ikonomi le setšhaba.

src: The NIP provides catalytic projects that are meant to contribute towards the country’s long-term economic and social developmental goals.
tgt: NIP e kgontšha tlhabollo ya mararankodi a mananeokgoparara a naga ao a sepelelanago le Foreimweke ya Bosetšhaba ya Tlhabollo ya Mafelo gape le Sekao sa Tlhabollo ya Selete (DDM).

src: The NIP provides for the development of the country’s infrastructure networks that are aligned to the National Spatial Development Framework and the District Development Model (DDM).
tgt: Leano la Kabo ya Kgase ya Petroliamo yeo e Fetošitšwego Seela (LPG) Kabinete e fetišitše go phatlalatšwa ga Leano la Kabo ya LPG la 2022 ka Kuranteng ya Mmušo gore setšhaba se fane ka ditshwayatshwayo mabapi le lona.

src: It also focuses the construction of infrastructure towards socio-economic development, and also to generate employment and broad-based black economic empowerment opportunities.
tgt: Leano le le lebeletše go ba le mohola tabeng ya go šomana le dihlotlo tša enetši ka mo nageng.

src: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Rollout Strategy of 2022.
tgt: Leano le šomana le, gareng ga tše dingwe, sebopego sa mmakete wa gabjale wa LPG, mananeokgoparara ao a šetšego a le gona, mokgwa wa go bea diporeisi gape le bokgoni bja tšweletšo ka bontšhi bjoo naga e nago le bjona bja go dira mabotlelo a dikgase tša LPLeano le šomana gape le lesolo la polokego le temogo ya gore kgase e bonwe bjalo ka sedirišwa seo se loketšego tikologo.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the LPG Rollout Strategy of 2022 in the Government Gazette for public comment.
tgt: Leanotekolo la Intaseteri ya Mebaene ya Afrika Borwa Kabinete e fetišitše Leanotekolo la Intaseteri ya Mebaene ya Afrika Borwa.

src: The strategy seeks to contribute towards addressing the country’s energy supply challenges.
tgt: Leano le tla, gareng ga tše dingwe, tla ka dikimollo ka leaning la yona la phethagatšo gore go be le sethalwa seo se nago le dintlha ka moka sa thutalefase go hlabolla datha ya thutalefase ya naga.

src: The strategy deals with, amongst others, the structural features of the current LPG market, existing infrastructure, the pricing structure and the current local manufacturing capacity of the LPG cylinders.
tgt: Leano le šišinya gape tšhomišanommogo gareng ga Kgoro ya Diminerale le Enetši le Koporase ya Tlhabollo ya Intaseteri go netefatša gore tekolo e kgontšha go akaretšwa ga dikhamphani tšeo di golago tša go šoma ka tekolo.

src: The strategy also deals with the safety and awareness campaign to raise the profile of domestic gas as an environmentally friendly fuel.
tgt: Le matlafatša gape karolo ya diphatišišo yeo e tlo tšewago ke ditheo tša diphatišišo tše bjalo ka MINTEK le Lekgotla la Diphatišišo tša Saense le Intaseteri, mmogo le lenaneo la tlhabollo ya mabokgoni.

src: Amendment to the policy on high-demand spectrum and the policy direction on the licensing of a wireless open access network (WOAN) Cabinet approved the amendmentof the policy on high-demand spectrum and the policy direction on the licensing of a WOAN to be published for public comment.
tgt: Sekhwama sa Matlafatšo sa Bosetšhaba se rwele maikarabelo a lefela mašeleng a go bengdithekisi ka moka bao ba lego molaong ebile ba nago le dilaensense tša go šoma ka dithekisi, gomme go balwa tšona dithekisi, dithekisi tša go ba le dimitara gape le dithekisi tša go bitšwa ka inthanete.

src: The proposed amendments remove the requirements to license the WOACabinet had in 2019 approved this policy on high-demand spectrum and the policy direction on the licensing of a WOAN to give effect to the Electronic Communications Act, 2005 (Act 36 of 2005).
tgt: Molaokakanywaphetošo wa Poso ya Afrika Borwa (SAPO) wa 2021 Kabinete e fetišitše go phatlalatšwa ga Molaokakanywaphetošo wa SAPO gore setšhaba se fane ka ditshwayatshwayo mabapi le wona.

src: The National Empowerment Fund is responsible for the disbursement of the compensation to all legal taxi operators with valid operating licences, including minibus-taxis, metered taxis and e-hailing partners.
tgt: E tla ba moabaditirelo tša poso le khoria wa maemo a lefase tirelo ya tshepedišo ya dithoto yeo e logagantšwego kgwebo ka inthanete, gomme gape e tla ba mothopo wa ditšithale bakeng sa kgwebo le ditšhaba.

src: South African Post Office (SAPO) Amendment Bill of 2021.
tgt: Diphetošo tšeo di šišintšwego, tšeo di sepelelanago le Pego ya Pholisi ya Bosetšhaba yeo e Logagantšwego ya ICT ya 2016, le tšona di kaonafatša mokgwapušo wa SAPMolaokakanywaphetošo wa Panka ya Poso ya Afrika Borwa wa 2021 Kabinete e fetišitše go išwa ga Molaokakanywaphetošo wa Panka ya Poso ya Afrika Borwa wa 2021 Palamenteng.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the SAPO Amendment Bill for public comment.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o fetoša Molao wa Panka ya Poso wa 2010 (Molao wa bo 9 wa 2010) gore o sepelelane le Molao wa Dipanka wa 1990 (Molao wa bo 94 wa 1990).

src: It will be a service provider of a universal postal and courier an integrated logistics e-commerce, and will be a digital hub for business and communities.
tgt: Ge o se no amogelwa go ba Molao, gona Panka ya Poso e tla kgona go šoma bjalo ka lekala leo le ikemetšego ebile le nago le melao ya lona ya go šoma le se ka tlase ga SAPMolaokakanywa wa Sekhwama sa Taolo ya Ditšhila tšeo di Lego Kotsi Kabinete e fetišitše go phatlalatšwa ga Molaokakanywa wa Sekhwama sa Taolo ya Ditšhila tšeo di lego Kotsi gore setšhaba se fane ka ditshwayatshwayo mabapi le wona.

src: The proposed amendments, which are aligned to the National Integrated ICT Policy White Paper of 2016, also make improvements to the governance provisions of the SAPSouth African Postbank Amendment Bill of 20.1 Cabinet approved the submission of the South African Postbank Amendment Bill of 2021 to Parliament.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o kgontšha go hlangwa ga sekhwama bjalo ka ge go laetšwe ke Pholisi ya Taolo ya Ditšhila tšeo di lego Kotsi.

src: The inaugural Presidential Imbizo of 2022 provides a platform for the President to engage with communities on their experiences of daily life and service delivery by government.
tgt: Letšatši la Ditokelo tša Botho Kabinete e amogela dipoledišano le ditiragalo tšeo di tšwelago pele bjalo ka karolo ya go keteka Letšatši la Ditokelo tša Botho la ngwageng wo ka la 21 Hlakola 2022 ka tlase ga moeno wo: “Ngwaga wa Botee le Mpshafatšo: Go Šireletša le go Lota Diphihlelelo tša rena tša Ditokelo tša Botho”.

src: CongratulationsCabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to the: South African Women’s cricket team, who are flying the national flag high at the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup in New Zealand.
tgt: Matshidišo Kabinete e rometše matshidišo go ba lapa le bagwera ba::Morena Mandla Ka-Mabuza (47), motaki, moanegi ebile e le Mopresidente wa maloba wa South African Students’ Congress (Sasco).

src: He was the former public servant in the Department of Public Works and Infrastructure.
tgt: Yena o kile a ba mohlankedi wa setšhaba ka Kgorong ya Mešomo ya Setšhaba le Mananeokgoparara.

src: Appointments All appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Go Thwalwa Batho ka moka bao ba thwetšwego mešomong mangwalo a bona a dithuto a tla tiišetšwa le go netefatšwa ka maleba.

src: Mr Zane-Udien Dangor as DG at the Department of International Relations and Cooperation.
tgt: Morena Zane-Udien Dangor Molaodipharephare ka Kgorong ya Dikamano le Tšhomišano ya Boditšhabatšhaba.

src: Ms Phindile Patronella Mkwanazi as Deputy DG: Learning and Profssional Development at the National School of Government.
tgt: Mme Phindile Patronella Mkwanazi bjalo ka Motlatša-Molaodipharephare ka lekaleng la Tlabollo ya Go Ithuta le Boprofešenale ka Sekolongtlhahlo sa Mmušo sa Bosetšhaba.

src: Mr David Mamphitha as Chief Executive Officer of the Mine Health and Safety Council.
tgt: Morena David Mamphitha bjalo ka Hlogophethiši ya Lekgotla la Polokego ya Maphelo ka Mebaeneng.

src: Persons to serve in the International Air Services Council:
tgt: Batho bao ba tlo šomelago Lekgotla la Ditirelo tša Difofane tša Boditšhabatšhaba:

src: Ms Nomveliso Ntanjana (Chairperson) Mr Nare Thupana (Vice Chairperson) Mr Grant Reagon Son Mr Tumelo Chipfupa and Ms Pfumelani Dorcas Mbulayeni.
tgt: Mme Nomveliso Ntanjana (Modulasetulo) Morena Nare Thupana (Motlatšamodulasetulo) Morena Grant Reagon Son Morena Tumelo Chipfupa le Mme Pfumelani Dorcas Mbulayeni.

src: Persons to serve in the Air Services Licensing Council:
tgt: Batho bao ba tlo šomelago Lekgotla la Kabo ya Dilaesense tša Ditirelo tša Difofane:

src: Mr Leroy Musa Nsibande (Chairperson) Ms Raesibe Sharon Kekana (Vice Chairperson) Mr Rickie Rodger Rennie
tgt: Morena Leroy Musa Nsibande (Modulasetulo) Mme Raesibe Sharon Kekana (Motlatšamodulasetulo) Morena Rickie Rodger Rennie

src: Ms Zonica Leanda Mtshali and
tgt: Mme Zonica Leanda Mtshali le

src: The South African Government responded to the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) global pandemic by declaring the National State of Disaster in March 2020, in terms of the Disaster Management Act, 2002 (Act 57 of 2002).
tgt: Merero e Bohlokwa Seemong sa Bjale Seemo sa Masetlapelo sa Bosetšhaba Mmušo wa Afrika Borwa o ikarabetše go leuba leo le phatlaletšego le lefase la Bolwetši bja Kokwanahloko ya Khorona (COVID-19) ka go goeletša Seemo sa Masetlapelo sa Bosetšhaba ka Hlakola 2020, go ya le ka Molao wa Taolo ya Masetlapelo wa 2002 (Molao wa bo 57 wa 2002).

src: This facilitated an integrated and coordinated response to save lives and livelihoods.
tgt: Se se ile sa kgontšha karabelo yeo e logagantšwego ebile e kgokaganego go boloka maphelo le boitekanelo.

src: The country has been under regulations of the National State of Disaster on COVID-19 since March 2020, when South Africa recorded its first cases of the virus.
tgt: Naga e bile ka tlase ga melawana ya Seemo sa Masetlapelo sa Bosetšhaba ka baka la COVID-19 go tloga ka Hlakola 2020 ge Afrika Borwa e be e eba le motho wa mathomo yoo a nago le kokwanahloko ye.

src: The President has announced further interventions that are meant to get the country to embark on a new phase in the management of the COVID-19 pandemic.
tgt: Mopresidente o tsebišitše dikimollo tše dingwe gape tšeo di lebeletšwego go bea naga legatong le leswa ge go etla taolong ya leuba la COVID-19.

src: The recent extension of the National State of Disaster to 15 April 2022 takes into consideration the need to continue augmenting the existing legislation and contingency arrangements undertaken by organs of state to address the impact of the disaster.
tgt: Katološo yeo e sa tšwago go dirwa ya Seemo sa Masetlapelo sa Bosetšhaba go fihla ka la 15 Moranang 2022 e lemoga bohlokwa bja go tšwela pele go oketša melawana yeo e lego gona le dipeakanyo tša komanamadulaabapile ka makala a mmušo go šomana le ditlamorago tša masetlapelo.

src: Cabinet has called for the consideration of health regulations to regulate non-pharmaceutical safety measures such as the wearing of masks, social distancing, limits for gatherings and vaccinations.
tgt: Kabinete e dirile boipiletšo bja gore melawana ya tša polokego ya maphelo e latelwe, e bjalo ka go apara maske, go bula sekgoba, go se fete palo ye itseng ya dikgobokano, mmogo le go entela.

src: They will also allow us to set up emergency, rapid and effective response systems to mitigate the severity of COVID-.
tgt: Melawana ye e tla kgona gape go re kgontšha gore re hlame mananeo a tša tšhoganetšo le karabelo go fokotša go gakala ga COVID-19.

src: COVID-19 vaccination.
tgt: Go Entela Kgahlanong le COVID-19 Kabinete e gopoditše batho ka moka ka Afrika Borwa go tšwela pele go ntšha mahlo dinameng bjale ka ge re sešo re fenya COVID-19, ya ba ya ipiletša go bao ba nago le mengwaga e 12 le go feta go yo entela.

src: Cabinet reminded all people in South Africa to remain vigilant as COVID-19 has not yet been defeated, and called on those aged 12 years and older to vaccinate.
tgt: Go entela e sa dutše e le sona sebetša se sekaonekaone kgahlanong le kokwanahloko, gomme go fokotša kotsi ya go lwala kudu, go robala bookelong le lehu.

src: Vaccination remains our best defence against the virus, and reduces the risk of serious illness, hospitalisation and death.
tgt: Le ge palo ya diphetetšo le mahu e le fase gabjale, re lebagane le kgonagalo ya lephoto la bohlano mo dibekeng tše di tlago.

src: The only defence we have is the scientific evidence showing the power of vaccines to save lives.
tgt: Sebetša sa rena se tee seo re nago le sona ke bohlatse bja saense bjoo bo bontšhago maatla a meento ya COVID-19.

src: Our country has already administered over 33 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccines.
tgt: Naga ya borena e šetše e hlabetše ditšhwaana tše dimilione tše 33 tša meento ya COVID-19.

src: Cabinet further welcomed the Code of Practice on the management of COVID-19 exposure in the workplace issued by the Department of Employment and Labour.
tgt: Kabinete e tšwetše pele ya amogela Molawanatšhomo ge go etla taolong ya go bewa pepeneneng ga COVID-19 ka mafelong a mošomo, woo o phatlaladitšwego ke Kgoro ya Mešomo le Bašomi.

src: The Code of Practice was developed following public consultation with the National Economic Development and Labour Council and will take effect when the National State of Disaster is lifted.
tgt: Molawanatšhomo o hlamilwe go latela dipoledišano tša setšhaba le Lekgotla la Bosetšhaba la Tlhabollo ya Ikonomi le Bašomi, gomme o tla phethagatšwa ge Seemo sa Masetlapelo sa Bosetšhaba se fedišwa.

src: The Code of Practice will guide employers and employees in conducting or updating a risk assessment plan to limit COVID-19 infections in the workplace.
tgt: Molawanatšhomo o tla hlahla bengmešomo le bašomi ge ba dira goba ba mpshafatša leano la tekolo ya dikotsi go fokotša diphetetšo tša COVID-19 ka mafelong a mošomo.

src: It lists measures such as vaccination, social distancing and personal hygiene to safeguard workspaces.
tgt: O hlalosa mekgwa e bjalo ka go entela, go bula sekgoba le go hlweka, elego tšeo di ka dirwago go hlokomela mafelo a mošomo.

src: South Africa Investment Conference (SAIC).
tgt: Kopano ya tša Peeletšo ya Afrika Borwa (SAIC).

src: Cabinet welcomed delegates from across the country and world to the fourth SAIC taking place on Thursday, 24 March 2022 in Johannesburg.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše dikemedi go tšwa ka mo nageng le lefaseng ka bophara kopanong ya bone ya SAIC yeo e tlo bago ka la 24 Hlakola 2022 go la Johannesburg.

src: The conference is showcasing the many investment opportunities and comparative advantages that South Africa offers investors, in a period of growing African integration through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which promotes intra-African trade.
tgt: Kopano e laetša menyetla e mentšhi ya peeletšo mmogo le dibaka tšeo Afrika Borwa e di fago, mo nakong ya kgokaganyo ya Afrika ka Kgwebišano yeo e Lokologilego ka Kontinenteng ya Afrika (AfCFTA) yeo e tšweletšago pele kgwebišano ka gare ga Afrika.

src: Local and foreign investments play an important role in growing our economy and creating sustainable jobs.
tgt: Dipeeletšo tša ka mo gae le tša go tšwa ka ntle ga naga di raloka karolo e bohlokwa kgodišong ya ikonomi ya borena le go hlola mešomo yeo e swarelelago.

src: The SAIC spurs a cycle of economic activity, employment and consumer demand that can support the growth trajectory of the country.
tgt: Kopano ya SAIC e hlohleletša mešongwana ya ikonomi, mešomo le nyakego ya badiriši tšeo di ka thekgago tsela ya kgolo ya naga.

src: Our past investment conferences have attracted a total of R774 billion in commitments.
tgt: Dikopano tša rena tšeo di fetilego tša peeletšo di gokeditše dibilione tše 744 tša diranta tšeo di ikgafetšwego.

src: Of the 152 investment projects announced, 45 have already been completed and a further 57 are under construction.
tgt: Go diprotšeke tše 152 tša dipeeletšo tšeo di tsebišitšwego, tše 45 di šetše di phethilwe gomme tše dingwe gape tše 57 di sa agwa.

src: Cabinet is confident that this year’s conference will build on our investment tally, as part of our nation’s drive to attract R.2 trillion in investment over five years.
tgt: Kabinete e na le boitshepo bja gore kopano ya ngwageng o e tla ikaga go tšwa motheong wa rena wa peeletšo, bjalo ka karolo ya lesolo la setšhaba sa borena go goketša dipeeletšo tša diranta tše ditrilione tše mo mengwageng e mehlano.

src: Impact of the Russia and Ukraine conflict on the economy.
tgt: Seabe sa ntwa ya Russia le Ukraine go ikonomi Kabinete e lekola seabe seo ntwa yeo e tšwelago pele gareng ga Russia le Ukraine e tlo bago le sona mo ikonoming ya naga, bjale ka ge ditlamorago tša yona di bonala ka mebarakeng ya ditšhelete le dithekong go phatlalala le lefase.

src: The best way to protect our economy and welfare of our people is to proceed with the implementation of the Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan (ERRP).
tgt: Tsela e kaonekaone ya go šireletša ikonomi ya rena le boitekanelo bja batho ba borena ke go tšwela pele ka phethagatšo ya Leano la Mpshafatšo le Tsošološo ya Ikonomi (ERRP).

src: Government is committed to using all of the levers at our disposal to cushion South Africans from the effects of the rising cost of living and ensure that our economy withstands these turbulent times.
tgt: Mmušo o ikgafile go šomiša didirišwa ka moka tšeo re nago le tšona go šireletša MaAfrika Borwa go ditlamorago tša seemo seo se gakalago sa ditheko le go netefatša gore ikonomi ya rena e kgona go kgotlelela dinako tše tše boima.

src: Auction of the high-demand radio frequency spectrum.
tgt: Go Rekišwa Okšeneng ga Maphoto a Seyalemoya ao a Nyakwago Kudu Kabinete e amogetše go phethwa ka katlego ga okšene ya mathomo ka nageng ya go rekišwa ga maphoto a seyalemoya ao a nyakwago kudu ka ba Bolaodi bjoo bo Ikemetšego bja Dikgokagano ka Afrika Borwa (ICASA).

src: Cabinet welcomed the successful conclusion of the country’s first auction of the high-demand radio frequency spectrum by the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa.
tgt: Lekgetho la dibilione tše tša diranta leo le kgobokeditšwego go tšwa okšeneng le tla išwa sekhwameng sa bosetšhaba gore le thekge ditlapele tša bosetšhaba tšeo di akaretšago kagoleswa ya ikonomi, go hlola mešomo yeo e hlokegago kudu, le go lwa le bomenetša, bosenyi, le dikgaruru tša bong le go bolawa ga basadi.

src: The R.4-billion revenue collected from the auction will go to the national fiscus to support our national priorities, which include rebuilding the economy, creating much-needed jobs, and fighting corruption, crime and gender-based violence and femicide.
tgt: Go ba gona ga lephoto leo le nyakegago kudu la tlaleletšo go tla akgofiša kabo ya ditheknolotši tše diswa tše bjalo ka 5G, go fokotša theko ya datha ya dillathekeng le go netefatša gore go ba le kgokagano e maatla ya inthanete.

src: The licensing of the new spectrum is accompanied by agreed social obligations to connect public schools, health facilities and police stations over the next three years.
tgt: Go abelwa laesense ga lephoto le leswa go sepela le boitlamo bja go kgokaganya dikolo tša setšhaba, mafelo a tša maphelo le ditiši tša maphodisa mo nakong ya mengwaga e meraro yeo e tlago.

src: Cabinet thanked all South Africans for joining in the country’s Human Rights Day celebrations on Monday, 21 March 2022 under the theme: “The Year of National Unity and Renewal: Promoting and Protecting our Human Rights.”.
tgt: Letšatši la Ditokelo tša Botho Kabinete e lebogile MaAfrika Borwa ka moka ge a tsenetše meketeko ya Letšatši la Bosetšhaba la Ditokelo tša Botho ka Mošupologo wa la 21 Hlakola 2022 ka tlase ga moeno wo: “Ngwaga wa Botee le Mpshafatšo: Go Tšweletša pele le go Šireletša Ditokelo tša rena tša Botho”.

src: Advancing human rights in our country is a catalyst for nation-building, which is a process we must continue to nurture and defend at all times.
tgt: Go tšweletša pele ditokelo tša botho ka mo nageng ya rena ke sebetša sa go aga setšhaba, elego tshepedišo yeo re swanetšego go tšwela pele go e hlokomela le go e lwela ka dinako tšohle.

src: Through our diversity, we can strengthen our unity and build a cohesive society.
tgt: Ka go fapafapana ga rena, re ka matlafatša botee bja rena le go aga setšhaba seo se swaranego.

src: In the continuing spirit of working together, as we move towards Freedom Month in April, Cabinet called on all South Africans to renew our fight against racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and all related intolerances in their area of influence.
tgt: Ka moya woo o tšwelago pele wa go šoma mmogo, ge re le gare re lebile Kgweding ya Tokologo ka Moranang, Kabinete e ipileditše go MaAfrika Borwa ka moka go mpshafatša ntwa ya rena kgahlanong le semorafe, kgethollo ya semorafe, lehloyo la bafaladi le tšohle tše sa lokago tša go swana natšo ka makaleng ka moka ao di a huetšago.

src: Cabinet noted and congratulated the former Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo on being appointed as the new Chief Justice of South Africa, with effect from 1 April 2022, and wished him well in his new responsibilities.
tgt: Go Thwalwa ga Moahlodimogolo ka Afrika Borwa Kabinete e lemogile le go lebogiša Motlatša-Moahlodimogolo wa peleng, Moahlodi Raymond Zondo, ge a thwetšwe go ba Moahlodimogolo wa Afrika Borwa go tloga ka la 1 Moranang 2022, gomme ya mo akela mahlatse le mahlogonolo maikarabelong a gagwe a maswa.

src: Cabinet further noted President Cyril Ramaphosa’s intention to nominate Justice Mandisa Maya, the President of the Supreme Court of Appeal of South Africa, for the position of Deputy Chief Justice when it becomes vacant.
tgt: Kabinete e tšwetše pele ya lemoga maikemišetšo a Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa a go kgetha Moahlodi Mandisa Maya, yoo elego Mopresidente wa Kgorotsheko ya Boipobolo ya Afrika Borwa, go ba Motlatša-Moahlodimogolo ge sekgoba sa maemo ao se bulega.

src: Interim order granted on humantarian aid to the Republic of Cuba.
tgt: Taelo ya Nakwana yeo e Filwego Tabeng ya go thuša Ripaboliki ya Cuba Kabinete e lemogile taelo ya nakwana yeo e filwego ka Kgorongkgolo ya Tsheko ya Tshwane, yeo e emišago phethagatšo ya thušo yeo Afrika Borwa e dumetšego go e fa Rapaboliki ya Cuba.

src: The matter will again be before the courts in 20 days’ time and government will present its argument then.2 South Africa’s bonds of friendship with Cuba are deeply rooted in our region’s struggle for liberation.
tgt: Molato wo o tla boa gape kgorongtsheko mo matšatšing a 20 gomme mmušo o tla ala ngangišano ya wona nakong yeo.

src: Were it not for the selfless intervention of the Cubans in Southern Africa over three decades, it would have taken far longer to liberate this region from colonial oppression.
tgt: Bogwera bja Afrika Borwa le Cuba bo ikepetše ntweng ya tokologo ya selete sa rena.

src: Former President Nelson Mandela understood this, which is why Cuba was the first country outside the continent Madiba visited upon his release from prison in 1990.
tgt: Ge nkabe e se ka thušo go tšwa go batho ba Cuba ge ba imolla Borwa bja Afrika mo mengwageng ya go feta e 30, nkabe go tšeere nako e telele go lokolla selete se go tšwa kgatelelong ya bokoloneale.

src: Cuba made monumental sacrifices to fight alongside African liberation movements at a time when the small island nation had been struggling under the United States’ economic embargo for a decade and a half.
tgt: Mopresidente wa peleng, Nelson Mandela, o be a kwešiša se, gomme ke ka fao Cuba e bilego naga ya mathomo ka ntle ga kontinente yeo Madiba a e etetšego ge a se no lokollwa kgolegong ka 1990.

src: Cuba’s economic crisis has become untenable and the Cuban Government is in need of assistance.
tgt: Cuba e tloga e lahlegetšwe ke tše ntšhi ge e be e thuša mekgatlo ya tokologo ya ka Afrika nakong yeo naga ye ya sehlakahlaka se sennyane e be e tlaišega ka tlase ga mapheko ao Amerika e bego e a beile ikonoming ya yona mengwaga e lesomehlano.

src: Mexico, Bolivia and Russia are among the countries which have provided humanitarian aid to ease the island’s worst economic crisis in decades.
tgt: Mexico, Bolivia le Russia di gare ga dinaga tšeo di e filego thušo go nolofatša mathata a mabe go fetišiša a ikonomi ao sehlakahlaka se se bilego le ona mo mengwageng e mentšhi.

src: Cabinet this week joins in commemorating the Battle of Cuito Cuanavale in Angola that took place from 1987 to 1988.
tgt: Kabinete bekeng ye e tsenela meketeko ya go gopola Ntwa ya Cuito Cuanavale ka Angola, yeo e diregilego go tloga ka 1987 go fihla ka 1988.

src: Cuba played the critical role in assisting African liberation movements to realise their objectives.
tgt: Cuba e bapetše karolo e bohlokwa ka go thuša mekgatlo ya tokologo ya ka Afrika go lemoga dinepo tša yona.

src: There was no material gain for the Cubans who came to our support, but their overriding incentive was to fight for the liberation of Southern Africa from colonial and reactionary forces.
tgt: Ga go na seo batho ba Cuba ba holegilego ka sona ge ba be ba tlile go re thuša maikemišetšomagolo a bona e be e le go lwela tokologo ya Borwa bja Afrika go tšwa dinaleng tša bokoloneale.

src: Then President Fidel Castro was driven by revolutionary zeal and he told his comrades they were fighting “the most beautiful cause of mankind”.
tgt: Mopresidente Fidel Castro ka nako yeo o be a hlohleletšwa ke go nyaka go bona diphetogo, gomme o ile a botša makhomoreiti a gagwe gore ba lwela “selo se sebotse kudu go batho”.

src: From Angola to Namibia and Algeria to Guinea Bissau, Cuba played a decisive role in contributing to the liberation of these African countries from colonial occupation.
tgt: Go tloga Angola go ya Namibia, le go tloga Algeria go ya Guinea Bissau, Cuba e bapetše karolo e bohlokwa ka go kgatha tema tokologong ya dinaga tše tša Afrika go tšwa bokolonealeng.

src: Cuba has continued to consistently provide medical and other assistance to South Africa in the post-1994 period, most recently during the COVID-19 pandemic, and it is our moral obligation to show solidarity with the people of Cuba at a time when they are struggling to survive.
tgt: Cuba e tšwetše pele go fa Afrika Borwa meriana le thušo e nngwe ka morago ga 1994, le gonabjale ka nako ya leuba la COVID-19, gomme ke maikarabelo a rena a botho go bontšha gore re batee le batho ba Cuba mo nakong ye ele goreng e boima maphelong a bona.

src: Visit by His Majesty King Letsie III Cabinet noted and welcomed the courtesy call from His Majesty King Letsie III of the Kingdom of Lesotho to President Ramaphosa that took place on Friday, 18 March 2022 in Pretoria.
tgt: Ketelo ka Kgošikgolo Letsie III Kabinete e lemogile le go amogela ketelo ya Kgošikgolo Letsie III wa Lesotho go Mopresidente Ramaphosa, yeo e diregilego ka Labohlano la 18 Hlakola 2022 go la Tshwane.

src: President Ramaphosa, in his capacity as the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Facilitator to the Kingdom of Lesotho, exchanged views with His Majesty King Letsie III on bilateral relations and progress regarding the SADC facilitation process in the Kingdom of Lesotho.
tgt: Mopresidente Ramaphosa, ka maemo a gagwe bjalo ka Mokgokaganyi wa Southern African Development Community (SADC) go naga ya Lesotho, o ile a boledišana le Kgošikgolo Letsie III ka dikamano le tšwelopele mabapi le tshepedišo ya kgokaganyo ya SADC ka nageng ya Lesotho.

src: It is envisaged that Basotho, through the facilitation of President Ramaphosa, will work in earnest to complete the reforms process before holding the next general elections scheduled for September 2022.Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Go letetšwe gore Basotho, ka kgokagano ya Mopresidente Ramaphosa, ba tla šoma ka maatla go feleletša tshepedišo ya dimpshafatšo pele ba ka swara dikgethokakaretšo tša go latela, tšeo di beetšwego kgwedi ya Lewedi 2022.

src: Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Proft Shifting (BEPS MLI).
tgt: Diphetho tša Kabinete Kopano ya Dinaga ya Go Phethagatša Mekgwa ya Tumelelano ya Lekgetho go Thibela go Tšhabela Tefelo ya Lekgetho le Mekgwa ya go Efoga go Lefa Lekgetho (BEPS MLI) Kabinete e fetišitše go išwa ga BEPS MLI Palamenteng go yo fetišwa.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the BEPS MLI to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Bjalo ka e nngwe ya dinaga tše 95 tšeo di kgathago tema ka tumelelanong yeo e thomilwego ke Mokgatlo wa Tšhomišanommogo le Tlhabollo ya Ikonomi (OECD) go fokotša menyetla ya go tšhabela lekgetho le mekgwa yeo e sa lokago ya go hlokomologa lekgetho ka dikhamphani tša boditšhabatšhaba, Afrika Borwa e saenne tumelelano ya lekgetho ka Phupu 2017.

src: As one of the 95 countries participating in the convention initiated by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) to reduce opportunities for tax avoidance and base erosion by multinational companies, South Africa signed the tax treaty in June 2017.
tgt: Ge tumelelano ya lekgetho e se no fetišwa, Afrika Borwa e tla e šomiša mmogo le ditumelelano tše dingwe tšeo e di saennego le dinaga tše dingwe.

src: Once the tax treaty is ratified, South Africa will apply it alongside other tax treaties it has signed with other countries.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ke leloko la OECD gomme e ikgafile go šoma le dinaga tše dingwe go emiša mašokotšo a dikhamphani ao a ntšhwago ka mo nageng go išwa mafelong ao a lefelago lekgetho la tlase goba a sa le lefelego.

src: South Africa is a member of the OECD and is committed to working with other countries to stop company profits being artificially shifted out of the country to low or no tax environment.
tgt: Phetošo ya Tshepedišo ya Tumelelano ya Lekgetho gareng ga Afrika Borwa le Kuwait Kabinete e fetišitše go išwa Palamenteng ga Tshepedišo ya Tumelelano ya Lekgetho yeo e saennwego gareng ga Afrika Borwa le Kuwait.

src: Amendments to this treaty, which came into force in 2006, were made and signed in 2021.
tgt: Diphetošo go tumelelano ye, yeo e thomilego go šoma ka 2006, di dirilwe le go saenelwa ka 2021.

src: The tax protocol deals with the avoidance of double taxation and prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income between the two countries.
tgt: Tshepedišo ya lekgetho e šomana le go efoga go lefa lekgetho gabedi le go thibela go tsenya letsogo koketšong ya sekhwama sa naga ge go etla makgethong a meputso magareng ga dinaga tše tše pedi.

src: Apart from dealing with tax evasion, such treaties seek to encourage tax transparency between countries.
tgt: Ntle le go šomana le go tšhabela lekgetho, ditumelelano tša mohuta wo di lebeletše go hlohleletša go se khute ga tša lekgetho gareng ga dinaga.

src: Integrated Crime and Violence Prevention Strategy (ICVPS).
tgt: Leano leo le Logagantšwego la Thibelo ya Bosenyi le Dikgaruru (ICVPS).

src: Cabinet approved the ICVPS for implementation.
tgt: Kabinete e fetišitše ICVPS gore e phethagatšwe.

src: The strategy will serve as an implementation tool of the White Paper on Safety and Security adopted in 2016.
tgt: Leano le le tla šoma bjalo ka sedirišwa sa phethagatšo sa Pego ya tša Polokego le Tšhireletšo yeo e amogetšwego ka 2016.

src: It advocates for a whole of government and society approach in fighting crime and preventing violence.
tgt: Yona e thekga taba ya gore mmušo ka moka ga wona mmogo le setšhaba go lweng le bosenyi le go thibeleng dikgaruru.

src: The ICVPS consists of six interdependent and interrelated pillars namely, (1) an effective criminal justice (2) early interventions in preventing crime (3) victim support interventions (4) effective and integrated service delivery (5) safety through environmental design and (6) active public and community participation.
tgt: ICVPS e na le dikokwane tše tshela tšeo di thekganago ebile di amanago, gomme tšona ke, (1) toka yeo e šomago ka go phethagala kgahlanong le bosenyi (2) dikimollo tša ka pela thibelong ya bosenyi (3) dikimollo tša thekgo ya batšwasehlabelo (4) kabo ya ditirelo yeo e šomago ka go phethagala ebile e logagantšwego (5) polokego ka tlhamego ya tikologo le (6) go kgatha tema ga setšhaba ka mafolofolo.

src: The strategy acknowledges the need for complimentary interventions to address the drivers of crime such as poverty, inequality, unemployment, social welfare health and education.
tgt: Leano le le lemoga tlhokego ya dikimollo tšeo di lokologilego go šomana le dilo tšeo di hlohleletšago bosenyi tše bjalo ka bohloki, go se lekalekane, tlhokego ya mešomo, boitekanelo bja leago, tša maphelo le thuto.

src: It is inclusive in terms of both urban and rural areas, including traditional councils, as stakeholders.
tgt: Lona le a akaretša go ya le ka metsesetoropo le metsemagae, go balwa le makgotla a ka mošate, bjalo ka batšeakarolo.

src: It has been fully consulted with all the spheres of government, business, research institutions and civil-society organisations.
tgt: Go boledišanwe ka botlalo le makala ka moka a mmušo, dikgwebo, ditheo tša diphatišišo le mekgatlo ya setšhaba.

src: The approved strategy replaces the current National Crime Prevention Strategy.
tgt: Leano leo le fetišitšwego le tsena legatong la Leano la Bosetšhaba la Thibelo ya Bosenyi leo le šomago gabjale.

src: South Africa’s Country Investment Strategy (CIS).
tgt: Leano la Naga ya Afrika Borwa la Peeletšo (CIS).

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the CIS for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e fetišitše go phatlalatšwa ga CIS gore setšhaba se fane ka ditshwayatshwayo go lona.

src: The strategy seeks to position the country as a key African investment destination of choice by leveraging quality foreign and domestic direct investments.
tgt: Leano le le lebeletše go bea naga maemong a go ba lefelo le bohlokwa la dipeeletšo ka Afrika ka go šomiša ka botlalo dipeeletšo tša boleng tša go tšwa dinageng dišele le ka mo gae.

src: The strategy is anchored on the country’s priority investment and economic development sectors such as
tgt: Leano le itheile ka peeletšo ye bohlokwa ya naga le makala a tlhabollo ya ikonomi a bjalo ka

src: finance, insurance, real estate and business services (ii) transport and logistics, (iii) manufacturing (iv) mining and quarrying,
tgt: ditšhelete, inšorense, dintlo le ditsha, le ditirelo tša kgwebo (ii) dinamelwa le tshepetšo ya dithoto, (iii) tšweletšobontšhi (iv) mebaene le go epa

src: electricity, gas and water, and (vi) agriculture and agro-processing.
tgt: mohlagase, kgase le meetse, le (vi) temo le botswaki bja ditšweletšwa tša temo.

src: It provides investment mechanisms to attract small, medium and micro enterprises into the economic growth drive.
tgt: Le tla ka mekgwa ya peeletšo go goketša dikgwebo tše nnyane, tša magareng le tše nnyanennyane go ba ka lesolong la kgolo ya ikonomi.

src: The strategy also taps into a number of multilateral, regional and bilateral agreements which South Africa has signed.
tgt: Leano le tsenya letsogo le ka ditumelelanong tša palo ya go bonala tša selete le dinaga tšeo Afrika Borwa e di saennego.

src: The strategy is aligned to the goals of the National Development Plan, ERRP, Re-imagined Industrial Strategy and the recently adopted National Infrastructure Plan 2050.
tgt: Leano le amana le dinepo tša Leano la Bosetšhaba la Tlhabollo, ERRP, Leano leo le Lebeletšwego Leswa la Diintaseteri mmogo le Leano la Bosetšhaba la Mananeokgoparara la 2050 leo le sa tšwago go amogelwa.

src: The nine provinces and their eight respective metropolitan key economies are central in driving the strategy, which will be a living document that will constantly be adaptable to the changing economic environment.
tgt: Diprofense tše senyane mmogo le ditoropo tša tšona tšeo di swerego ikonomi di beilwe pele tabeng ya go sepetša leano le, leo e tlo bago tokomane yeo e feletšego yeo e tlo kgonago go fetoga le mabaka a ikonomi.

src: Revised National Biodiversity Framework (NBF).
tgt: Lenaneo la Bosetšhaba leo le Mpshafaditšwego la Diphedi ka go fapafapana ga tšona (NBF) Kabinete e fetišitše NBF gore e phethagatšwe.

src: The NBF, which Cabinet approved for public consultation in November 2020, was developed in line with the National Environmental Management: Biodiversity Act, 2004 (Act 10 of 2004).
tgt: NBF, yeo Kabinete e e fetišitšego gore e sekasekwe ke setšhaba ka Dibatsela 2020, e hlamilwe go ya le ka Molao wa Bosetšhaba wa Taolo ya Tikologo: wa Diphedi ka go fapafapana ga tšona wa 2004 (Molao wa bo 10 wa 2004).

src: It provides for an integrated, coordinated and uniform approach to biodiversity management by all organs of state, non-governmental organisations (NGOs), the private sector and communities.
tgt: E tla le ka mokgwa woo o logagantšwego, o kgokaganego ebile o swanago taolong ya diphedi ka go fapafapana ga tšona ka makala ka moka a mmušo, mekgatlo yeo esego ya mmušo (di-NGO), lekala la poraefete mmogo le ditšhaba.

src: In 2018, the South African National Biodiversity Institute conducted a comprehensive scientific assessment of the state of biodiversity and ecosystem in South Africa.
tgt: Ka 2018 Setheo sa Bosetšhaba sa Diphedi ka go fapafapana ga tšona sa Afrika Borwa se dirile tekolo yeo e tseneletšego ya saense mabapi le seemo sa diphedi le lefase ka Afrika Borwa.

src: The revised NBF sectoral plan of action addresses the threats identified from this assessment.
tgt: Leanotšhomo leo le mpshafaditšwego la NBF le šomana le matšhošetši ao a laeditšwego go tšwa tekolong ye.

src: The revised framework was consulted with all the spheres of government state-owned entities (SOEs), conservationist entities NGOs and local communities.
tgt: Lenaneo leo le mpshafaditšwego go boledišanwe ka lona makaleng ka moka a mmušo, dikgwebong tša mmušo, ditheong tša bolotatikologo di-NGO le ditšhabeng tša ka mo gae.

src: The implementation of the NBF is guided by the adopted National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (2015-2025).
tgt: Phethagatšo ya NBF e hlahlwa ke Leano le Leanotšhomo la Bosetšhaba la Diphedi ka go fapafapana ga tšona leo le amogetšwego (la 2015-2025).

src: South Africa is a signatory to the United Nations’ Convention on Biological Diversity, which promotes the conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ke yona e rwelego marapo ka go United Nations’ Convention on Biological Diversity, yeo e tšweletšago pele go lotwa ga diphedi ka go fapafapana ga tšona, tšhomišo yeo e swarelelago ya dikarolo tša lona, le kabelano yeo e lekanago ya diputseletšo tšeo di tšwago didirišweng tša tšenethiki.

src: Draft National Spatial Development Framework (NSDF).
tgt: Sethalwa sa Lenaneo la Bosetšhaba la Tlhabollo ya Dikgoba (NSDF).

src: Cabinet approved the draft NSDF for implementation.
tgt: Kabinete e fetišitše sethalwa sa NSDF gore se phethagatšwe.

src: It was prepared in terms of the Spatial Planning and Land Use Management Act, 2013 (Act 16 of 2013) and approved for public consultation in 2019.
tgt: Sona se beakantšwe go ya le ka Molao wa Peakanyo ya Dikgoba le Taolo ya Tšhomišo ya Naga wa 2013 (Molao wa bo 16 wa 2013) gomme sa fetišwa gore setšhaba se fane ka ditshwayatshwayo go sona ka 2019.

src: Inputs were obtained from various stakeholders, including professional bodies, all spheres of government, SOEs and members of the public.
tgt: Dikakanyo di hweditšwe go tšwa go batšeakarolo ba go fapafapana, go balwa le mekgatlo ya mešomo ya profešenale, makala ka moka a mmušo, dikgwebo tša mmušo le maloko a setšhaba.

src: The framework seeks to deal with the eradication of the colonial and apartheid spatial legacies in an orderly and coordinated manner.
tgt: Lenaneo le lebeletše go šomana le go fediša ditlamorago tša tšhomišo ya dikgoba tša bokoloneale le tša mmušo wa kgethollo ka tsela ya maswanedi.

src: It provides a long-term spatially focused developmental approach towards planning and a land use management system.
tgt: Lona le tla ka tsela yeo e nepilego tlhabollong ya dikgoba yeo e išago peakanyong le mokgwataolong wa tšhomišo ya naga.

src: The document will be accessible through the website of the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (WEBTOKEN).
tgt: Tokomane e tla humanega websaeteng ya Kgoro ya Temo, Pušetšo ya Naga le Tlhabollo ya Metsemagae (WEBTOKEN).

src: Cabinet approved the Official Identity Management Policy, following an extensive public consultation in 2021.
tgt: Pholisi ya Semmušo ya Taolo ya Boitsebišo Kabinete e fetišitše Pholisi ya Semmušo ya Taolo ya Boitsebišo go latela dipoledišano tšeo di tseneletšego le setšhaba ka 2021.

src: This policy will replace the current Identification Act, 1997 (Act 68 of 1997), which establishes the National Population Register (NPR) and also specify its scope in the mandatory records that are captured on it.
tgt: Pholisi ye e tla tsena legatong la Molao wa Boitsebišo wa 1997 (Molao wa bo 68 wa 1997) woo o šomago gabjale, woo o hlamago Lenaneo Bosetšhaba la Go Ngwadiša Batho (NPR), gape le go hlalosa ka botlalo mošomo wa wona ka direkotong tša kgapeletšo tšeo di beilwego go lona.

src: This Act is not aligned to the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination and human dignity.
tgt: Molao wo ga o sepelelane le dikokwane tša Molaotheo ya tekatekano, go se kgethologanye mmogo le seriti sa motho.

src: The adopted policy proposes a single digital NPR of all people – irrespective of citizenship and sex status – who live and have lived in the country.
tgt: Pholisi yeo e fetišitšwego e šišinya NPR e tee ya ditšithale ya batho ka moka – go sa balwe gore ke ba ka mo nageng goba aowa, le gore ke ba bong bofe – bao ba dulago ebile ba kilego ba dula ka mo nageng.

src: It also provides for a biometric National Identity System (NIS) that will enable a single view of a person.
tgt: E tla gape le ka Mokgwa wa Boitsebišo wa Bosetšhaba (NIS) woo o tlo kgontšhago go lebelelwa dintlha tša motho yo tee fela.

src: The NIS will also be able to interface with other government and private sector identity systems.
tgt: NIS e tla kgona gape go šomišana le mekgwa e mengwe ya boitsebišo ka mmušong le ka lekaleng la poraefete.

src: The policy will also ensure the protection of the rights of members of the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Intersex, Queer and Asexual community.
tgt: Pholisi e tla netefatša gape tšhireletšo ya ditokelo tša maloko a setšhaba sa Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Intersex, Queer le Asexual.

src: White Paper on Marriages in South Africa.
tgt: Pego ya Manyalo ka Afrika Borwa Kabinete e fetišitše Pego ya Manyalo ka Afrika Borwa gore e phethagatšwe.

src: Cabinet approved the White Paper on Marriages in South Africa for implementation.
tgt: Pego e arabela dikahlolo tše dintšhi tša dikgorotsheko tšeo di humanego dikarolwana tše dingwe tša melao ya gabjale ya manyalo di sa sepelelane le Molaotheo.

src: The White Paper responds to many court judgements that have found some elements of the current marriage legislation to be unconstitutional.
tgt: Yona e beakantše manyalo ka moka gore a phethwe go ya le ka dikokwane tša tekatekano, go se kgetholle le seriti sa motho bjale ka ge seo se boletšwe ka Molaotheong wa Ripaboliki ya Afrika Borwa wa 1996.

src: It has aligned all marriages to be concluded in accordance with the principles of equality, non-discrimination and human dignity as provided for in the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: Pego yeo e fetišitšwego e tla dumelela MaAfrika Borwa le badudi ka moka ba mehuta ka moka ya bong, ditumelo le ditšo ka moka go phetha dikamano tša semolao go ya le ka dikokwane tša Molaotheo.

src: The approved White Paper will allow South Africans and residents of all sexual orientations, religious and cultural persuasions to conclude legal unions in line with the constitutional principles.
tgt: Pego e ala tše dingwe tša dikamano tšeo di sa akaretšwago bjalo ka manyalo a bana gape le manyalo ao a dirwago monglenyalo wa bobedi a sego.

src: Cabinet approved the OSBP and its implementation strategy.
tgt: Pholisi ya Dikgoro tša go tsena ka Nageng (OSBP) Kabinete e fetišitše OSBP le leanophethagatšo la yona.

src: The policy seeks to harmonise the movement of people and goods between South Africa’s land ports of entry and its neighbouring countries.
tgt: Pholisi e lebeletše go sepetša ka mokgwa o tee go sepela ga batho le dithoto gareng ga dikgoro tša go tsena ka Afrika Borwa le dinaga-baagišane.

src: It gives effect to the One-Stop Border Framework that was adopted by Cabinet in 2018.
tgt: Yona e fa Lenaneo la Dikgoro tša go tsena ka nageng leo le amogetšwego ke Kabinete ka 2018.

src: The application of the policy will alleviate current congestions at our land ports of entry for cross-border travellers and traders.
tgt: Phethagatšo ya pholisi e tla fediša sephethephethe sa gabjale dikgorong tša go tsena ka nageng sa baeti le bagwebišani.

src: These interventions are also key in the country’s efforts in driving the AfCFTA agreement.
tgt: Dikimollo tše ebile gape di bohlokwa maitekelong a naga a go sepetša tumelelano ya AfCFTGe e se no šoma ka botlalo ebile e na le melao ya maleba mmogo le tlhabollo ya mananeokgoparara, re lebeletše gore tshepedišo ya dithoto, dinamelwa le batho e tla dirwa ka mokgwa wo bonolo wa ka pela.

src: Cabinet approved the transitional hosting of the Presidential Climate Commission by the National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac).
tgt: Go swarwa ga Nakwana ga Komišene ya Mopresidente ya Tša Klaemete Kabinete e fetišitše go swarwa ga Komišene ya Mopresidente ya Tša Klaemete ke ba Lekgotla la Bosetšhaba la Tlhabollo ya Ikonomi le Mešomo (Nedlac).

src: Nedlac will host the commission with its secretariat for two years or shorter to enable the promulgation of the Climate Change Act.
tgt: Nedlac e tla swara komišene e na le bongwaledi bja yona mengwaga e mebedi goba go se fete fao go kgontšha go tsebišwa ga Molao wa Phetogo ya Klaemete.

src: The period will also afford the commission – in collaboration with the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment – to finalise the feasibility study and business case for the future establishment of the commission as determined by the Climate Change Bill.
tgt: Nako yeo e tla kgontšha komišene – ka tšhomišano le Kgoro ya Dithokgwa, Boreahlapi le Tikologo – go feleletša dinyakišišo tša go lekola seo se hlokegago gape le tša kgwebo bakeng sa go hlangwa ga komišene ka moso go ya le ka Molaokakanywa wa Phetogo ya Klaemete.

src: Draft White Paper on National Rail Policy.
tgt: Sethalwa sa Pego ya Pholisi ya Bosetšhaba ya Ditimela Kabinete e fetišitše sethalwa sa Pholisi ya Bosetšhaba ya Ditimela.

src: The policy will guide in creating an efficient transport system that will be able to compete locally and internationally.
tgt: Pholisi e tla hlahla ge go etla tlhamong ya mokgwa wa dinamelwa woo o šomago ka go phethagala woo ka kgonago go phadišana ka mo gae le maemong a boditšhabatšhaba.

src: The policy proposes focused interventions that will promote investments in both the feight and passenger services.
tgt: Pholisi e šišinya dikimollo tšeo di tla tšweletšago pele dipeeletšo ka ditirelong tša dithoto le go rwala batho.

src: It will also improve rural access and increase mobility to promote economic growth.
tgt: E tla re gape ya kaonafatša phihlelelo ka dinagamagae ya ba ya oketša mesepelo go tšweletša pele kgolo ya ikonomi.

src: It will also contribute substantially towards reducing the country’s emissions as it proposes rail genetic technologies in upgrading the rail stock.
tgt: E tla re gape ya tsenya letsogo tabeng ya go fokotša go tupa ga muši ka ge e šišinya ditheknolotši tša tšenethiki tša ditimela tlhabollong ya ditimela.

src: The policy will be made public once the Department of Transport has published it in the Government Gazette.
tgt: Pholisi e tla humanega ge Kgoro ya Dinamelwa e se no e phatlalatša ka Kuranteng ya Mmušo.

src: Independent Municipal Demarcation Authority (IMDA) Bill of 2022.
tgt: Molaokakanywa Molaokakanywa wa Bolaodi bjoo bo Ikemetšego bja Mellwane ya Mebasepala (IMDA) wa 2022 Kabinete e fetišitše go išwa ga Molaokakanywa wa IMDA wa 2022 Palamenteng go yo sekasekwa go tsenelela.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the IMDA Bill of 2022 to Parliament for further processing.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o phatlaladitšwe gore setšhaba se fane ka ditshwayatshwayo go wona ka Phupu 2020, gape le dipoledišano ka ditshwayatshwayo tšeo di tšwago setšhabeng.

src: The Bill was published for public comment in June 2020 and subsequent engagements on the comments received from the public.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o hlalosa tshepedišo ya pušo ya IMDDitšhišinyo tša wona di akaretša go hlalosa ka botlalo nako yeo maloko a Boto a tlo šomelago IMDA le gore a šoma mošomo wa nakwana, ntle le Modulasetulo yoo yena a ka e šomelago mehla le mehla.

src: It also guides the IMDA on the process towards the delimiting of boundaries.
tgt: O hlahla gape IMDA tshepedišong ya go bea mellwane.

src: President Ramaphosa will lead a delegation of Ministers to the World Expo Dubai in the United Arab Emirates on Monday, 28 March 2022.
tgt: Tiragalo yeo e sa Tlago Ketelo go la Middle East Mopresidente Ramaphosa o tla eta pele kemedi ya Ditona go ya go Pontšho ya go Tsenelwa ke Dinaga tša Lefase (World Expo) go la Dubai ka nageng ya United Arab Emirates ka Mošupologo wa la 28 Hlakola 2022.

src: South Africa is participating at the expo with a pavilion showcasing the country’s rich heritage and investment opportunities.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e kgatha tema ka pontšhong ka go ba le moagwana woo o bontšhago bohwa bjoo naga e humilego ka bjona mmogo le menyetla ya dipeeletšo.

src: CongratulationsCabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to the:the South African women’s cricket team, for flying the national flag high at the Women’s Cricket World Cup in New Zealand.
tgt: Melaetša Ditebogišo Kabinete e rometše ditebogišo le go akela mahlatse le mahlogonolo go: Sehlopha sa Afrika Borwa sa Basadi sa Khirikhethe, seo se phagamišitšego leina la Afrika Borwa phadišanong ya Sebjana sa Lefase sa ICC sa Khirikhethe ya Basadi go la New Zealand.

src: They defeated current World Champions England in their third match and have managed to win four matches in the tournament so far.
tgt: Bona ba fentše Dinkgwete tša gabjale tša Lefase elego England papading ya bona ya boraro, gomme ba kgonne go fenya dipapadi tše nne thonamenteng go fihla gabjale.

src: CondolencesCabinet joined President Ramaphosa in extending condolences to the government and people of the Republic of Zambia following the passing of former President Rupiah Bwezani Banda (85).Cabinet expressed condolences to the family and friends of:Mr Michael Spicer (68), the former Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Business Leadership South Africa, who played a significant role in forging a stronger relationship between business and WEBTOKEN Luzuko Koti (47), the former Director of Communication and Marketing at the Nelson Mandela Foundation and Business Manager of Channel Africa.
tgt: Matshidišo Kabinete mmogo le Mopresidente Ramaphosa ba rometše matshidišo go mmušo le batho ba Ripaboliki ya Zambia go latela go hlokofala ga Mopresidente wa peleng, Rupiah Bwezani Banda (85).

src: Mr Sheik Abdul Gamiet Gabier (86), Life President of the Muslim Judicial Council South Africa, who was a renowned scholar, community activist and a pioneer of the Al-Azhar Institute of Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e rometše matshidišo go ba lapa le bagwera ba: Morena Michael Spicer (68), Hlogophethiši (CEO) ya peleng ya Business Leadership South Africa, yoo a bapetšego karolo e bohlokwa ya go hlama kamano e tiilego gareng ga dikgwebo le mmušo.

src: Fourth South Africa Investment Conference (SAIC).
tgt: Khonferense ya Bone ya Afrika Borwa ya Dipeeletšo (SAIC).

src: Cabinet welcomed the successful conclusion of the fourth SAIC held at the Sandton Convention Centre, Johannesburg on Thursday, 24 March 2022, which saw domestic and international investors pledging new investments in our country.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše thumo ye atlegilego ya khonferense ya bone ya SAIC yeo e bego e swaretšwe gola Sandton Convention Centre, Johannesburg ka Labone, 24 Hlakola 2022, fao go yona babeeletši ba ka mo nageng le ba boditšhabatšhaba ba dirilego dikano tša dipeeletšo tše diswa ka mo nageng ya gaborena.

src: Our country received 80 new investment pledges totalling R332 billion.
tgt: Naga ya gaborena e amogetše dikano tša dipeeletšo tše 80 tša palomoka ya go lekana R322 bilione.

src: This takes the total investments pledged to R.14 trillion, which not only represents 95 percent of our investment target but also places us firmly on the path to exceed our R.2 trillion investment target over five years.
tgt: Se se hlatlošitše palomoka ya dipeeletšo go fihla R.14 trilione, yeo e sa laetšego fela 95% ya nepo ya dipeeletšo tša rena eupša e re bea maemong a go fetiša R.2 trilione ya nepo ya dipeeletšo tša rena mo mengwageng ye mehlano ye tlago.

src: These investment commitments affirm our country’s status as an investment destination of choice.
tgt: Maikgafo a a dipeeletšo a kgonthišiša seemo sa naga ya gaborena bjalo ka naga yeo batho ba ka kgethago go beeletša go yona.

src: So far, R316 billion of the commitments have been invested in 46 projects that have been completed and a further 57 projects that are still under construction.
tgt: Go fihla gabjale, R316 bilione ya maikgafo ao a dirilwego a beeleditšwe diprotšekeng tše 46 tšeo di phethagaditšwego ka botlalo le tše dingwe tše 57 tšeo di santšego di tšwelapele.

src: Cabinet notes the successes of past pledges as reported at the Conference, covering among others new production capacityin sectors as diverse as automobiles, food production, pharmaceuticals and digital centres.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile dikano tše di dirilwego kua morago goya le ka fao go filwego pego khonferenseng, tšeo di akaretšago magareng ga tše dingwe mabokgoni a maswa mo mafapheng a go fapafapana go swana le difatanaga, tšweletšo ya dijo, meriana ya ka dikhemising le disenthara tša titšithale.

src: Cabinet called on all sectors of society to support these critical interventions as we work together to reverse our unemployment rate, which climbed to percent, according to the Quarterly Labour Force Survey results released recently by Statistics South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e ipileditše go mafapha ka moka a setšhaba go thekga magatotharollo a a bohlokwa ge re le gare re šoma mmogo go theoša palo ya godimo ya tlhokego ya mešomo yeo e hlatlogetšego godimo go fihla go 35.3%, goya le ka dipoelo tša Dinyakišišokakaretšo tša Kotara le Kotara tša Dipalo tša Bašomi tšeo di lokolotšwego ke ba Dipalopalo tša Afrika Borwa malobanyana mo.

src: Lifting of the National State of Disaster Cabinet also welcomed the lifting of the National State of Disaster announced by President Cyril Ramaphosa on Monday, 4 April 2022.
tgt: Phedišo ya Maemo a Masetlapelo a Bosetšhaba Kabinete e amogetše go fedišwa ga Maemo a Masetlapelo a Bosetšhaba ao a tsebagaditšwego ke Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa ka Mošupologo, 4 Moranang 2022.

src: This milestone was made possible by the resilience of people in South African who complied with all Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) safety protocols designed by government to save lives and livelihoods.
tgt: Phenyo ye e kgonagetše ka baka la bopelotelele bja MaAfrika Borwa bao ba obametšego magato a polokego a Bolwetši bja Coronavirus (COVID-19) ao a hlamilwego ke mmušo go phološa maphelo le mekgwa yeo batho ba iphedišago ka yona.

src: The pandemic will henceforth be managed in terms of the National Health Act, 2003 (Act 61 of 2003).
tgt: Leuba le goyapele le tla laolwa goya ka Molao wa Bosetšhaba wa Maphelo, 2003, (Molao 61 wa 2003).

src: The draft health regulations that will inform the National Health Act of 2003 are open for public comment until 16 April 2022.
tgt: Seakanywa sa melao ya maphelo yeo e tlo hlamago Molao wa Bosetšhaba wa Maphelo wa 2003 se buletšwe batho ka moka go fihla ka 16 Moranang 2022.

src: Cabinet reminded all people in the country to continue taking the necessary preventative measures to safeguard ourselves and others against COVID-19 infections.
tgt: Kabinete e gopoditše batho ka moka ka mo nageng go tšwelapele go tšea magato a maleba a thibelo go itšhireletša le go šireletša ba bangwe kgahlanong le diphetelo tša COVID-19.

src: This includes regularly washing our hands with water and soap or using a 70% alcohol-based sanitiser, wearing a mask that covers both the nose and mouth when indoors, keeping a safe social distance of at least one metre, opening windows for ventilation and vaccinating.
tgt: Se se akaretša go hlapa matsogo a rena kgafetšakgafetša ka meetse le ka sesepe goba ka go šomiša sanithaesa sa diatla sa go tswakwa ka alekhohole ya go feta 70%, ka go apara dimaseke tša go pipa dinko le melomo ge ba le ka gare ga meago, ka go šielana sekgala se ka bago mithara o tee, ka go bula mafastere gore go tsene moya le ka go hlaba meento.

src: COVID-19 vaccinations are effective in preventing serious illness, hospitalisation and even death.
tgt: Meento ya COVID-19 e nale mohola ka go thibela malwetši a mašoro, go amogelwa maokelong le go efoga mahu a go hlolwa ke COVID-19.

src: Protect yourself and your loved ones by visiting your nearest vaccination site to get vaccinated for free, even without an appointment.
tgt: Itšhireletše o be o šireletše le bao o ba ratago ka go etela lefelo la kgauswi le wena la meento gore o yo hlaba moento ntle le tefo, ešita le ge o sena peakanyetšo ya goya go hlaba.

src: Migration to digital broadcasting.
tgt: Go Hudugela Kgašong ya Titšithale.

src: The deferment on the Analogue Switch-off Date from 31 March to 30 June 2022 provides sufficient time to government to complete the installation of set-top boxes (STBs) for households that have registered timeously and are entitled to receive them before the analogue switch-off.
tgt: Go fegwa ga Letšatši la go Tingwa ga Dikgašo tša Megala go tloga ka 31 Hlakola go fihla ka la 30 Phupu 2022 go fa mmušo nako ye lekanego ya go phethagatša ka botlalo go lokelwa ga mapokisana a dikgašo tša ditšithale (di-STB) go magae ao a ingwadišitšego ka nako ebile a nale maloka a go fiwa ona mapokisana ao pele ga ge dikgašo tša megala di tingwa.

src: The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies will ensure that all the 507 251 households that registered by 31 October 2021 are connected no later than 30 June 2022.
tgt: Kgoro ya Dikgokagano le ya Ditheknolotši tša Titšithale e tla netefatša gore magae ka moka a 507 251 ao a ingwadišitšego pele ga la 31 Diphalane 2021 a hlomeseditšwe dikgašo tše tša ditšithale pele ga la 30 Phupu 2022.

src: The 260 868 households that registered between 31 October 2021 and 10 March 2022 will be connected to their STBs by 30 September 2022.
tgt: Magae a 260 868 ao a ingwadišitšego magareng ga la 31 Diphalane 2021 le la 10 Hlakola 2022 a tlo kgokaganywa dikgašong tša titšithale ka mapokisana a bona a di-STB pele ga la 30 Lewedi 2022.

src: Cabinet is confident that the completion of this process will support the process of digital migration and the subsequent release of the high frequency spectrum.
tgt: Kabinete e nale boitshepho bja gore phethagatšo ya kgato ye e tla thekga tshepedišo ya go fetogela kgašong ya titšithale gotee le maphoto a maemo a godimodimo a diyalemoya ao a tlo lokollwago ka morago.

src: Fighting crime and corruption Cabinet congratulated the country’s new National Commissioner of Police, General Sehlahle Fannie Masemola, following his recent appointment by President Ramaphosa.
tgt: Go Lwantšha Bosenyi le Bomenenene Kabinete e lebogišitše Mokhomišinare wo moswa wa Bosetšhaba wa Maphodisa wa naga, Jenerale Sehlahle Fannie Masemola, morago ga thwalo ya gagwe malobanyana mo ka Mopresidente Ramaphosa.

src: General Masemola has an outstanding record of achievements in policing across South Africa.
tgt: Jenerale Masemola o nale rekhoto ya maemo a godimo ya go fihlelela dimaka go tša sephodisa go ralala Afrika Borwa.

src: Cabinet welcomed the preservation orders granted to the Asset Forfeiture Unit of the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) by the Gauteng High Court against those involved in ‘financing’ the purchase of Optimum Coal Mine for R.1-billion in 2016 by the Gupta-owned Tegeta Exploration and Resources company.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše ditaelo tša kiletšo tšeo di filwego Yuniti ya Kamogo ya Dithoto ya Lekgotla la Bosetšhaba la Bosekiši (NPA) ka Kgorotsheko ya Godimo ya Gauteng kgahlanong le bao ba amegago go thekga ka ditšhelete go rekwa ga Moepo wa Malahla wa Optimum ka R.1 bilione ka 2016 ka khamphani ya go laolwa ke lapa la ga Gupta ya go bitšwa Tegeta Exploration and Resources.

src: The rulings, which demonstrate the effective coordinated approach of the NPA and the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation of the South African Police Service, send a strong message about the growing capacity of government to deal with State Capture and ensure accountability for those involved – and to seize, recover and return stolen money.
tgt: Diphetho tše tša kgorotsheko, tša go laetša lemanoga le nago le mohola la go logelwa maano ke NPA le Lebotho la Sephodisa sa Afrika Borwa la Nyakišišo ya Melato ya Maemo a Godimo, di romela molaetša wo bogale mabapi le mabokgoni a mmušo ao a golelago godimo a go swaragana le go Gogwa ga Mmušo ka Nko le go netefatša gore bao ba amegago ba rwešwa maikarabelo a mediro ya bona – le gape go amoga, go hwetša le go bušetša morago ditšhelete tše utswitšwego.

src: In holding those involved in corruption accountable, Cabinet also welcomed the judgement by the Palm Ridge Specialised Commercial Crimes Court in Gauteng against a former Eskom financial controller for defrauding the power utility of R35 million by loading fake invoices for coal transport and the initiatives to recover the stolen monies.
tgt: Ka gona go dira gore bao ba amegago bosenying ba ikarabele medirong ya bona, Kabinete e amogetše kahlolo ka Kgorotsheko ya Palm Ridge ya Bosenyi bja Kgwebo bja Moswananoši gola Gauteng kgahlanong le molaodi wa peleng wa ditšhelete wa Eskom ka go timeletša R35 milione go tšwa khamphaning ye ya kabo ya mohlagase ka go ithomela mananeotheko a bofora a go sepetšwa ga malahlaka dinamelwa gotee le maitekelo a go hwetša tšhelete yeo e utswitšwego.

src: As an important milestone in our nation’s fight against corruption, Cabinet welcomed the handover of the fourth part of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry into State Capture Report.
tgt: Bjalo ka phenyo ye bohlokwa mo phenkgišanong ya setšhaba sa gaborena ya go lwantšha bomenemene, Kabinete e amogetše neeletšo ya karolo ya bone ya pego ya Khomišene ya Dinyakišišo ya Tirelo ya Semolao go tsinkelela go Gogwa ga Mmušo ka Nko.

src: President Ramaphosa will present to Parliament interventions to implement the commission’s recommendations when he submits the full report by 30 June 2022.
tgt: Mopresidente Ramaphosa o tla hlagišetša Palamente magatotharollo a go phethagatša ditšhišinyo tša khomišene ge a romela pego ye feletšego ka botlalo ka la 30 Phupu 2022.

src: Southern African Development Community (SADC) Extraordinary Organ Troika Summit.
tgt: Samiti ye sa Tlwaelegago ya Setho sa Troika ya Ditšhaba tšeo di Hlabologago tša Borwa bja Afrika (SADC) Kabinete e amogetše dipoelo tša Samiti ye sa Tlwaelegago ya Setho sa Troika ye swaretšwego gola Pretoria ka Mošupologo wa la 4 le ka Labobedi la 5 Moranang 2022.

src: Cabinet welcomed the outcomes of SADC Extraordinary Organ Troika Summit held in Pretoria on Monday, 4 and Tuesday, 5 April 2022.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ebile naga ya go swara samiti ye bjalo ka Modulasetulo wa Setho sa SADC go tša Dipolotiki, Boiphemelo le Tirišano ya Tšhireletšego.

src: The country’s tenure runs from August 2021 to August 2022.
tgt: Monyetla wa naga ye wa go tsorama setulo se o thoma ka Phato 2021 go fihla ka Phato 2022.

src: The summit received, among others, the SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) progress report.
tgt: Samiti ye e amogetše, magareng ga tše dingwe, pego ya mošomo wo dirilwego Morerong wa SADC gola Mozambique (SAMIM).

src: The SAMIM was deployed to support Mozambique to combat terrorism and acts of violent extremism.
tgt: Lebotho la sešole la SAMIM le rometšwe ka nageng ya Mozambique go lwantšha matšhošetši le ditiragalo tša dikgaruru tša go dirwa ka boomo.

src: Economy Cabinet welcomed credit rating agency Moody’s upgrade of its outlook on South Africa to stable from negative and the decision to affirm South Africa’s long-term foreign and local currency debt ratings at ‘Ba2’.
tgt: Ikonomi Kabinete e amogetše tlhatlošo ya kemedi ya kelo ya dikoloto e bago Moody ka ponelopele ya yona ya Afrika Borwa gore e tieletše go tšwa seemong sa go se kgahliše le sephetho sa yona sa go kgonthišiša gore dikelo tša dikoloto tša Afrika Borwa tša kharensi ya nako ye telele ya dinagadišele le ya ka mo nageng di tlogelwa maemong a ‘Ba2’.

src: The upgrade affirms the work of government to restore sustainability to the country’s public finances, which is supported by better-than-expected revenue collection.
tgt: Tlhatlošo ye e kgonthišiša mošomo wa mmušo wa go bušetša sekeng tielelo matlotlong a mmušo a naga ye, ya go thekgwa ke kgoboketšo ya lekgetho ya go šoma gabotse go fetiša ka fao go bego go letetšwe ka gona.

src: Revenue results for the period April 2021 to March 2022, showed that the South African Revenue Service collected more than R.5 trillion.
tgt: Dipoelo tša lekgetho tša go thoma ka Moranang 2021 go fihla ka Hlakola 2022, di laeditše gore ba Ditirelo tša Lekgetho la Afrika Borwa ba kgobokeditše tšhelete ya go feta R.5 trilione.

src: It represents a 25 percent improvement over the previous year and a 15 percent increase over the last year prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
tgt: Tšhelete ye e laetša kaonafatšo ya 25% mo ngwageng wa go feta le tlhatlogo ya 15% ka ngwaga wa mafelelo pele ga leuba la COVID-19.

src: Government is using the additional revenue to accelerate debt stabilisation and address urgent social needs, promote job creation through the Presidential Youth Employment Initiative, and support the public health sector.
tgt: Mmušo o šomiša lekgetho la tlaleletšo go akgofiša go bewa ga dikoloto ka fase ga taolo le go kalokana le dinyakwa tša tšhoganyetšo tša leago, go hlohleletša tlhomo ya mešomo ka Lesolo la Mopresidente la go Thwalwa ga Baswa, le go thekga lefapha la mmušo la tša maphelo.

src: Freedom Month.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Tokologo.

src: South Africa this year celebrates Freedom Month in April with renewed hope for a better tomorrow, having endured two sombre years under the global COVID-19 pandemic.
tgt: Ngwaga wo Afrika Borwa e keteka Kgwedi ya Tokologo ka Moranang ka tshepho ye mpshafaditšwego ya bokamoso bjo kaone, ka baka la ge e fetile mengwaga ye mebedi ya masetlapelo ka baka la leuba la lefase ka bophara la COVID-19.

src: The annual Freedom Day will be commemorated on Wednesday, 27 April 2022.
tgt: Letšatši le la Tokologo la Ngwaga ka Ngwaga le tla ketekwa ka Laboraro, 27 Moranang 2022.

src: Freedom Month commemorates and salutes all those whose sacrifices made it possible for us to enjoy the human rights and freedoms contained in our world-acclaimed Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: Ka Letšatši la Tokologo go ketekwa le go rolela kefa batho ka moka bao ka go ikuna ga bona tše ntši ba dirilego gore go kgonagale gore re ipshine ka ditokelo tša botho le tokologo yeo e lego ka gare ga Molaotheo wa go hlomphega kudu lefaseng wa Rephabliki ya Afrika Borwa wa 1996.

src: Cabinet called on all South Africans to work together as we continue our struggle to overcome the impact of COVID-19.
tgt: Kabinete e dirile boipiletšo go MaAfrika Borwa ka moka go šoma mmogo ge re le gare re tšwelapele ka phenkgišano ya rena ya go fekeetša ditlamorago tša COVID-19.

src: We all need to do our part to restore our economy, through the Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan, and grow more businesses to be able to create more jobs.
tgt: Ka moka re swanetše go kgatha tema ya rena go bušetša seemo sa ikonomi sekeng, ka Leano la Kagoleswa ya Ikonomi le go Boetšwa Sekeng ga yona, le go godiša dikgwebo tše dingwe tše ntši gore di tle di kgone go hloma mešomo ye mengwe ye mentši.

src: Holy Month of Ramadan Cabinet wished South Africa’s Muslim community a blessed Holy Month of Ramadan.
tgt: Kgwedi ye Kgethwa ya Ramadan Kabinete e lakaleditše setšhaba sa Afrika Borwa sa Mamoslemo Kgwedi ye Kgethwa ya dišegofatšo ya Ramadan.

src: Ramadan is annually marked around the world with prayer, fasting and acts of charity.
tgt: Ramadan e ketekwa ngwaga ka ngwaga go potologa lefase ka dithapelo, go ikuna dijo le ditiragalo tša dipelo tše borutho.

src: The Muslim community is an integral part of our national diversity and of our national character.
tgt: Setšhaba sa Mamoslemo ke karolo ye bohlokwa ya ditšo tša rena tša go fapafapana le semelo sa rena sa bosetšhaba.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diphetho tša Kabinete.

src: Draft National Integrated Small Enterprise Development (NISED) Masterplan.
tgt: Seakanywa sa Leano la Makgonatšohle sa Tlhabollo ya Bosetšhaba ya Dikgwepotlana tša Mohlakanelwa (NISED) Kabinete e dumeletše go phatlalatšwa ga Seakanywa sa NISED sa Leano la Makgonatšohle gore setšhaba se fe ditshwayotshwayo tša sona.

src: The initial Integrated Strategy for Entrepreneurship and Small Enterprises was adopted in 2005.
tgt: Leanopeakanyo la mathomo la Mohlakanelwa le Bogwebi le Dikgwebo tše Nnyane le amogetšwe ka 2005.

src: The strategy and the subsequent NISED give effect to the 1995 White Paper on National Strategy for the Development and Promotion of Small Business in South Africa.
tgt: Leanopeakanyo le le NISED ya go tla ka morago ga lona le kgontšha Sengwalwa sa 1995 sa Makgoraditsela godimo ga Leanopeakanyo la Bosetšhaba Tlhabollong le Tlhohleletšong ya Kgwebo mo Afrika Borwa.

src: Once adopted the NISED will replace the current Integrated Strategy for Entrepreneurship and Small Enterprises.
tgt: Ge e šetše e amogetšwe, NISED e tla tšeela legato Leanopeakanyo la bjale la Mohlakanelwa la Bogwebi le Dikgwebo tše Nnyane.

src: It will provide a coordination framework for all key ecosystem role players in small enterprise development.
tgt: E tla fana ka tlhako ya tsamaišo go bakgathatema ka moka ba bohlokwa ba mo kamanong ye tlhabollong ya dikgwebo tše nnyane.

src: It guides the coordinating mechanism that will guide all programmes that support small enterprises.
tgt: Yona e hlahla magato a tsamaišo ao a tlo hlahlago mananeo ka moka a go thekga dikgwebo tše nnyane.

src: This strategy seeks to increase the participation of small enterprises in the formal economy, eliminate red tape and promote the ease of doing business, particularly for small entrepreneurs.
tgt: Leanopeakanyo le le šetšane le go atiša go kgatha tema ga dikgwebo tše nnyane ka ikonoming ya go lefišwa metšhelo, go fediša magatotshepedišo a go rarela le go hlohleletša go dirwa ga dikgwebo moroba, kudukudu bahlomi ba dikgwebo tše nnyane.

src: The NISED is the product of a wide consultation with the relevant departments in the national, provincial and local spheres of government, business, labour, academics and various relevant institutions.
tgt: NISED ke lenaneo leo le hlotšwego ke ditherišano tša motlalanaga gotee le dikgoro tše maleba didikong tša mmušo tša bosetšhaba, tša profense le tša pušoselegae, dikgwebo, bašomi, dirutegi le ditheo tše maleba tša go fapafapana.

src: Incorporation of the Small Enterprise Finance Agency (SEFA) and Cooperative Banks Development Agency (CBDA) into the Small Enterprise Development Agency (SEDA).
tgt: Go tsenyeletšwa ga Etšensi ya Ditšhelete ya Dikgwebo tše Nnyane (SEFA) le Etšensi ya Tlhabollo ya Dipankaseboka (CBDA) ka gare ga Etšensi ya Tlhabollo ya Dikgwebo tše Nnyane (SEDA).

src: Cabinet approved the 20 months extension period for the merging of the two entities, the SEFA and CBDA, into the SEDThe merger was initially set to be effective from 1 April 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše katološo ya dikgwedi tše 20 ya go kopantšhwa ga makalakgwebo a mabedi, ebago SEFA le CBDA ka gare ga SEDKopanyo ye mathomong e be e theilwe gore e thome go tsenywa tirišong go tloga ka la 1 Moranang 2022.

src: This was after Cabinet approved the mergers to ensure government provides a single entity that will support its work in supporting small to medium enterprises and cooperatives.
tgt: Kopanyo ye e bile ka morago ga gore Kabinete e dumelele kopanyo ye go netefatša gore mmušo o hloma lekalakgwebo le tee leo le tla kgonago go thekga mošomo wa yona wa go thekga dikgwebo tše nnyane go fihla go tša magareng gotee le dikhamphani.

src: The approved extension will enable the Department of Small Business Development to finalise the legislative review to provide a proper legislated and policy environment that allows the formation of the single entity – SEDA single and well-resourced entity will provide a more streamlined support to small to medium enterprises and cooperatives.
