tgt: Ditsenogare tšeo di dirilwego ke Leano la Kaonafatšo le Kagolefsa ya Ekonomi (ERRP) di fokoditše kudu naga go dikhuetšo tša boditšhabatšhaba, gape tša šireletša mešomo le letseno.

src: Government’s strong economic interventions are beginning to bear fruit, as evidenced in Stats SA’s recent Quarterly Labour Force Survey results, which showed that over 648 000 jobs were gained between the first and second quarters of 2022.
tgt: Ditsenogare tše maatla tša ekonomi tša mmušo di thoma go tšweletša dipoelo tše dibotse, bjale ka ge go hlatsetšwe ka go dipoelo tša Dinyakišišo tša Bašomi tša Kotara ye nngwe le ye nngwe tša Stats SA, tšeo di bontšhitšego gore go bile le mešomo ye 648 000 mo kotareng ya mathomo le ya bobedi tša 2022.Diphetho tša Kabinete.

src: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Framework for the National Youth Policy (NYP).
tgt: Tlhako ya Tlhahlobo le Tekolo (M&E) ya Pholisi ya Bafsa ya Setšhaba (NYP).

src: Cabinet approved the M&E framework that will enable the effective monitoring and impact assessment of the pillars of the NYP 2020-2030.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše tlhako ya M&E yeo e tla kgontšhago tlhahlobo le kelo ya khuetšo ya dintlha tša bohlokwa tša NYP ya 2020-2030.

src: The framework provides five high-level indicators which are aligned with the pillars of the NYThe indicators were developed with the relevant stakeholders who have an interest in the development and empowerment of youth in the country.
tgt: Tlhako e fa ditaetši tša legato la godimo tše hlano tšeo di sepelelanago le dintlha tša bohlokwa tša NYDitaetši di dirilwe le bakgathatema ba maleba bao ba nago le kgahlego mo tlhabollong le matlafatšong ya bafsa ka mo nageng.

src: The data collection will be disaggregated in terms of age, gender, disability, racial grouping and the geographic setting of these interventions.
tgt: Tshedimošo e tla kgoboketšwa ka go aroganywa ka dikarolo go ya ka mengwaga, bong, bogolofadi, sehlopha sa merafe le tikologo ya thutafase ya ditsenogare tše.

src: The monitoring will be done in all spheres of government, entities and the private sector.
tgt: Dikgato tše tša go dira ditlhahlobo di tla dirwa ka mafelong ka moka a mmušo, ka ditheong ka moka le lekaleng la praebete.

src: The reports will be generated quarterly and published twice a year.
tgt: Dipego tša tšona di tla dirwa kotareng ye nngwe le ye nngwe gomme tša phatlalatšwa gabedi ka ngwaga.

src: Policy Framework for Integrated Planning.
tgt: Tlhako ya Pholisi ya Peakanyo ye e Kopantšwego.

src: Cabinet has approved the Policy Framework for Integrated Planning in government, which seeks to address the identified policy planning gaps in the current planning system.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše Tlhako ya Pholisi ya Peakanyo ye e Kopantšwego ya mmušo, yeo e nyakago go šogana le mafokodi a peakanyo ya pholisi ao a utollotšwego mo lenaneong la peakanyo la gonabjale.

src: The proposed interventions will amongst others deal with the lack of planning alignment within the three spheres of government.
tgt: Ditsenogare tšeo di šišintšwego di tla re gare ga tše dingwe tša šogana le tlhokego ya tlhopo ya peakanyo mo dikarolong tše tharo tša mmušo.

src: The interventions will introduce an evidence-based monitoring mechanism.
tgt: Ditsenogare di tla tsebiša mokgwa wa tlhahlobo wo o theilwego go bohlatse.

src: The policy framework also introduces easier predictability with long to medium and short-term planning across government.
tgt: Tlhako ya pholisi e tsebišitše gape kakanyo ye bonolo ka peakanyo ya nako ye telele go ya magareng le peakanyo ya nako ye kopana go phatlalala le mmušo.

src: It will work towards introducing legislative reforms to improve coherency and predictability in government planning and monitoring.
tgt: E tla šomela go thoma dimpshafatšo tša melao go kaonafatša kopano le kakanyo mo peakanyong le tlhahlobong ya mmušo.

src: Ratification of the Treaty for the Establishment of the African Medicines Agency (AMA).
tgt: Tumelelo ya Tumelelano ya go Thongwa ga Mokgatlo wa Dihlare tša Seafrika (AMA).

src: Cabinet approved the signing of the Treaty for the Establishment of the AMA and its submission to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go saenwa ga Tumelelano ya go Thongwa ga AMA le go išwa ga yona Palamenteng go ka dumelelwa.

src: This will give effect to the treaty that was adopted by the African Union Assembly in 2019.
tgt: Se se tla phetha tumelelano yeo e amogelwago ke Kopano ya Tumelelano ya Afrika ka 2019.

src: The treaty formally establishes the AMA for the continent.
tgt: Tumelelano e thoma semmušo AMA ya kontinente.

src: The agency will regulate medical products, and improve the safety and efficacy of the medical products for the continent.
tgt: Mokgatlo o tla laola ditšweletšwa tša dihlare, gomme wa kaonafatša polokego le bokgoni bja ditšweletšwa tša dihlare ka kontinenteng.

src: The signing and ratifying of this treaty will advance South Africa’s global and continental commitment toward strengthening the continental regulatory system on its health products.
tgt: Go saenwa le go dumelelwa ga tumelelano ye go tla kaonafatša boikgafo bja Afrika Borwa mo lefaseng le mo kontinenteng mo go matlafatšeng lenaneo la taolo ya kontinente mo go ditšweletšwa tša maphelo.

src: Report on the Performance of the Research and Development (R&D) Tax Incentive Programme – 2019/20 and 2020/2.
tgt: Pego ka ga Lenaneo la Tlhohleletšo ya Motšhelo la Phethagatšo ya Dinyakišišo le Tlhabollo (R&D) – 2019/20 le 2020/2.

src: Cabinet approved the submission to Parliament of the R&D Tax incentive Programme for the past two years (2019/20 and 2020/21).
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go išwa ga Lenaneo la tlhohleletšo ya Motšhelo la R&D Palamenteng mo mengwageng ye mebedi ya go feta (2019/20 le 2020/21).

src: This is in line with section 11D (17) of the Income Tax Act, 1962 (Act 58 1962), which requires the tabling of these reports in Parliament.
tgt: Se se sepelelana le karolo ya 11D (17) ya Molao wa Motšhelo wa Letseno, wa 1962 (Molao wa 58 wa 1962), woo o nyakago go alwa ga dipego tše ka Palamenteng.

src: The tax incentive programme seeks to encourage private companies to invest in R&D so as to stimulate investment growth.
tgt: Lenaneo la tlhohleletšo ya motšhelo le nyaka go hlohleletša dikhamphani tša praebete go beeletša mo go R&D gore go hlohleletšwe kgolo ya ekonomi, le go godiša katlego.

src: Cabinet is pleased that the report shows that new companies have applied for the tax incentive.
tgt: Kabinete e thabela gore pego e bontšha gore dikhamphani tše difsa di dirile kgopelo ya tlhohleletšo ya motšhelo.

src: It encourages more companies to access this scheme as part of growing their respective investment and stimulating economic growth.
tgt: E hlohleletša dikhamphani tše dintši go hwetša setlamo se bjalo ka karolo ya go godiša dipeeletšo tša bona le go hlohleletša kgolo ya ekonomi.

src: The top-four companies that accessed the tax incentive are in agro-processing mining beneficiation chemicals, cosmetics, pharmaceutical and electro-technical and Information Technology sectors that Cabinet endorsed as priority areas in the Industrial Policy Action Plan.
tgt: Dikhamphani tše nne tša godimo tšeo di hweditšego tlhohleletšo ya motšhelo di ka makaleng a tshepetšo ya ditšweletšwa tša temo kaonafatšo ya meepo dikhemikhale, dibotsefatši, dihlare le elektrotheknikhale le Theknolotši ya Tshedimošo tšeo Kabinete e di dumeletšego bjalo ka dikarolo tše bohlokwa mo Leanong la Katlego ya Pholisi ya Intasteri.

src: The full report can be accessed through the Department of Science and Innovation website: WEBTOKEAfrican Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) Forum – 2023.
tgt: Pego ka botlalo e ka hwetšwa mo wepsaeteng ya Kgoro ya Saense le Kaonofatšo: WEBTOKEForamo ya Molao wa Dibaka le Kgolo ya Afrika (AGOA) - 2023.

src: Cabinet has approved the hosting of the AGOA Forum in 2023.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go swarwa ga Foramo ya AGOA ka 2023.

src: AGOA was enacted by the United States of America (USA) in 2000 to provide unilateral trade preferential access for most of the sub-Saharan African countries and the USA domestic market.
tgt: AGOA e dumeletšwe ke Amerika (USA) ka 2000 go fa phihlelelo ya go ikgetha ya kgwebo ya go ikema go bontši bja dinaga tša Afrika tša Borwa bja Sahara le mebaraka ya gae ya USDikišontle tša Afrika Borwa ka fase ga AGOA di akaretša dienywa tša go butšwa, dimake, dikoloi, didirišwa, tšhipi, setala le ditšweletšwa tša khemikhale.

src: The actual date and venue are still to be announced.
tgt: Tšatšikgwedi la nnete le lefelo di sa tlo tsebišwa.

src: Group on Earth Observations (GEO) Ministerial Summit – 2023.
tgt: Samiti ya Ditona ya Sehlopha sa Ditlhahlobo tša Lefase (GEO) – 2023.

src: Cabinet approved that South Africa hosts the GEO Ministerial Summit in Cape Town in 2023.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše gore Afrika Borwa e sware Samiti ya Ditona ya GEO ka Motsekapa ka 2023.

src: The GEO is an intergovernmental body set up in 2003 after the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development.
tgt: GEO ke mokgatlo wa mebušo ya boditšhabatšhaba woo o hlomilwego ka 2003 ka morago ga Samiti ya Lefase ya Tlhabollo ya go Swarelela.

src: It serves as a multilateral platform where countries voluntarily contribute towards a common goal of building the GEO systems.
tgt: E šoma bjalo ka sefala sa kopano moo dinaga di kgathago tema ka go ithaopa go fihlelela nepo ya go swana ya go aga mananeo a GEGonabjale GEO e na le mebušo ya bosetšhaba ya go feta 113, ye 30 ya yona e tšwago ka Afrika gomme mekgatlo ye e ka bago 140 e kgatha tema, gomme ye 11 ya yona e tšwa Afrika.

src: South Africa has been an active Executive Committee member since 2005 and our scientists are currently participating in a number of research initiatives led through the GEOctober Transport Month (OTM) – 2022.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e dutše e le leloko la Komitiphethiši go tloga ka 2005 gomme boramahlale ba rena gonabjale ba kgatha tema mananeong a dinyakišišo a mmalwa ao a etilwego pele ke GEKgwedi ya Dinamelwa ya Diphalane (OTM) – 2022.

src: Cabinet approved the launching of the OTM campaign on Saturday, 1 October 2022, under the theme: “Sishov’ingolovane: together building transport infrastructure that builds and sustains livelihoods”.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go thakgolwa ga lesolo la OTM ka Mokibelo, 1 Diphalane 2022, ka fase ga morero: “Sishov’ingolovane: mmogo re aga infrastraktšha ya dinamelwa yeo e agago mešomo ya go swarelela”.

src: The annual OTM is used to raise awareness on transport as one of the critical elements in economic growth and spatial development.
tgt: OTM ya ngwaga le ngwaga e šomišwa go godiša temošo ka dinamelwa bjalo ka dikarolo tše bohlokwa mo kgolong ya ekonomi le tlhabollo ya mahlakore a mararo.

src: A number of activities will take place to showcase the various aspects of transport infrastructure in aviation, maritime, public transport and roads.
tgt: Go tla ba le ditiragalo tše mmalwa go bontšha dikarolo tše mmalwa tša infrastraktšha ya dinamelwa ka go difofane, dikepe, dinamelwa tša bohle le ditsela.

src: The activities will also raise awareness regarding transport safety and security.
tgt: Ditiragalo di lemoša gape ka polokego le tšhireletšo ya dinamelwa.

src: Stakeholder engagements will also be held to discuss various challenges in the transport sector.
tgt: Go tla akaretšwa gape bakgathatema go boledišana ka ditlhohlo tša go fapana mo lekaleng la dinamelwa.

src: Government remains committed to improving the country’s transport infrastructure, both in rural and urban areas, so as to facilitate an effective and efficient movement of goods and people.
tgt: Mmušo o dula o ikgafile mo go kaonafatšeng infrastraktšha ya dinamelwa ya naga, bobedi mo mafelong a segae le a setoropong, gore go sepetšwe tshepelo ye botse gape ya bokgoni ya dithoto le batho.

src: United Nations (UN) Human Settlement Programme Habitat (UN-HABITAT) Meeting.
tgt: Kopano ya Lenaneo la Magae la Bodulo bja Batho (UN-HABITAT) la Kopanoditšhaba (UN).

src: Cabinet has approved the hosting of the meeting of the members of the UN-HABITAT in Johannesburg on 16 and 17 October 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go swarwa ga kopano ya maloko a UN-HABITAT ka Johannesburg ka la 16 Diphalane 2022.

src: The Department of Human Settlements will coordinate this two-day meeting to be attended by political champions, practitioners and researchers, including key members of the Committee of Permanent Representatives of the UN-HABITAT based in Nairobi, Kenya.
tgt: Kgoro ya Bodulo bja Batho e tla sepetša kopano ye ya matšatši a mabedi yeo e tla tsenelwago ke ditsebi tša dipolotiki, ditsebi le banyakišiši, go akaretša malokomagolo a Komiti ya go ya go ile ya Baemedi ba UN-HABITAT bao ba lego Nairobi, Kenya.

src: Key issues to be discussed will include seeking transformational interventions for informal settlements and slums.
tgt: Ditaba tše bohlokwa tšeo go tla bolelwago ka tšona di tla akaretša ditsenogare tša phetogo go badudi ba mekhukhung le metsesetoropo go tlala kudu.

src: The outcomes of these deliberations will culminate in the launching of the Global Action Plan Framework, which will be tabled in the UN-HABITAT Assembly for endorsement in 2023.
tgt: Dipoelo tša dipoledišano tše di tla phethwa mo thakgolong ya Tlhako ya Leano la Katlego la Lefase, yeo e tla alwago Kopanong ya UN-HABITAT gore e dumelelwe ka 2023.Melaokakanywa.

src: National Council on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Bill of 2021.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wa Khansele ya Setšhaba ya Dikgaruru tša Bong le Dipolao tša Basadi le Bana (GBVF) wa 2021.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the National Council on GBVF Bill of 2021 to Parliament for processing.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go išwa ga Molaokakanywa wa Khansele ya Setšhaba ya 2021 Palamenteng gore go šoganwe le wona.

src: This Bill provides a legislative framework for the establishment of the statutory body to provide a focus intervention in dealing with GBVIt also provides for the establishment of the Board of the Council that will provide strategic leadership and oversee the implementation of the National Strategic Plan on GBVF, which was approved by Cabinet in October 2020 for implementation.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o fa tlhako ya molao mo go hlongweng ga mokgatlo wa molao gore go be le tsenogare ye e nepišago mo go šoganeng le GBVO dumelela gape go thongwa ga Boto ya Khansele yeo e tla fago taolo yeo e beakantšwego gomme ya laola phethagatšo ya Leano la Taolo ya Setšhaba ka ga GBVF, leo le dumeletšwego ke Kabinete ka Diphalane 2020 go phethagatšwa.

src: The board will have a 51% representation from civil society and 49% from government.
tgt: Boto e tla le kemedi ya 51 go tšwa go setšhaba sa gae le 49% go tšwa mmušong.

src: The Bill has already gone through public consultation.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o šetše o swayaswayilwe ke setšhaba.

src: Tobacco Products and Electronic Delivery Systems Control Bill of 2018.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wa Ditšweletšwa tša Motšoko le Didirišwa tša go Kgoga Motšoko tša Elektroniki wa 2018.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Tobacco Products and Electronic Delivery Systems Control Bill of 2018 to Parliament, which seeks to repeal the current Tobacco Products Control Act, 1993 (Act 83 of 1993), as amended.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go išwa palamenteng Ditshwayotshwayo tša Molaokakanywa wa Ditšweletšwa tša Motšoko le Didirišwa tša go Kgoga Motšoko tša Elektroniki wa 2018, tšeo di nyakago go phumola Molao wa gonabjale wa go Laola Ditšweletšwa tša Motšoko, (Molao wa 83 wa 1993) go ya le ka moo o mpshafaditšwego ka gona.

src: The Bill also seeks to strengthen the country’s public health measures and align them with the World Health Organisation Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o nyaka go matlafatša magato a maphelo a setšhaba a naga gomme o dire gore o sepelelane le Tumelelano ya Tlhako ya Mokgatlo wa Maphelo a Lefase ka ga Taolo ya Motšoko.

src: The Bill proposes, among others, 100% smoke-free indoor and some outdoor areas a ban on the sale of cigarettes through vending machines, and strengthens cigarette packaging and warning signage.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o šišinya gare ga tše dingwe, gore go se sa folelwa ka gare ga meago le mafelo a mangwe a ka ntle ga meago go fedišwa ga thekišo ya sekerete mo metšheneng ya go rekiša, le go thekga taba ya diphuthelwana tša disekerete le maswao a temošo.

src: The Bill has gone through extensive consultation with various stakeholders, including the tobacco industry, civil-society organisations and relevant government departments.
tgt: Molaokakanywa o fetišitšwe dikgatong tša go tsenelela tša go nyaka maikutlo a setšhaba a go fapana, go akaretša a intasteri ya metšoko, a mekgatlo ya badudi le a dikgoro tša mmušo tša maleba.

src: Upcoming Events.
tgt: Ditiragalo tše di Tlago.

src: 77th Session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA77) South Africa is participating in the UNGA77 taking place at the UN headquarters in New York City in the USA from 20 to 27 September 2022 under the theme: “A watershed moment: Unlocking transformative solutions to interlocking challenges”.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e kgatha tema ka go UNGA77 yeo e lego ka go dikantorokgolo tša UN ka Toropokgolong ya New York ka USA go tloga ka la 27 Lewedi 2022 ka fase ga morero: “Nako ya mathata: Go tšweletša ditharollo go kgokaganya ditlhohlo”.

src: For the global South, the economic and socio-economic impact of the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) pandemic has been disproportionate in relation to recovery in the developed North and this requires a united effort from all nations to ensure no one is left behind.
tgt: Go Borwa bja lefase, khuetšo ya ekonomi le ekonomi ya leago ya leuba la Bolwetši bja Coronavirus (COVID-19) e bile bothata kudu malebana le tsošološo go Leboa leo le hlabologilego gomme se se nyaka maitapišo ao a kopanetšwego go tšwa dinageng ka moka go kgonthiša gore ga go na yoo a tlogetšwego morago.

src: Preceding the UN General Debate, the UN Secretary-General, Mr António Guterres, will convene a summit on “Transforming Education” and host a high-level meeting focusing on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
tgt: Pele ga Ngangišano ya Kakaretšo ya UN, Mongwaledikakaretšo wa UN, Morena António Guterres, o tla beakanya samiti ka ga “Go fetoša Thuto” le go swara kopano ya maemo a godimo yeo e nepišago Dinepo tša Tlhabollo ya go Swarelela (di-SDG).

src: The SDGs meeting is expected to explore ways in which to regain momentum and accelerate their implementation.
tgt: Kopano ya di-SDG e swanelwa ke go nyakišiša ditsela tšeo go ka tsošološago maatla le go potlakiša phethagatšo.

src: Heritage Day.
tgt: Letšatši la Bohwa.

src: President Ramaphosa will deliver a keynote address at the 2022 National Heritage Day celebrations at the Union Buildings on Saturday, 24 September 2022.
tgt: Mopresidente Ramaphosa o tla fa polelokgolo mo meketekong ya Letšatši la Bohwa la Setšhaba mo Union Buildings ka Mokibelo, 24 Lewedi 2022.

src: The event will be held under the theme: “Celebrating the Legacy of Solomon Linda and South Africa’s Indigenous Music”.
tgt: Moletlo o tla swarwa ka fase ga morero: “Go keteka Bohwa bja Solomon Linda le Mmino wa Setšo wa Afrika Borwa”.

src: This year’s Heritage Month focuses on South Africa’s indigenous music with a spotlight on isicathamiya music and its immense contribution to our sport, arts, culture and heritage.
tgt: Kgwedi ye ya Bohwa e nepiša mmino wa setšo wa Afrika Borwa ka nepišo ya mmino wa Isicathamiya le tema yeo o ikgathago go dipapadi, bokgabo, setšo le bohwa.

src: The theme pays tribute to the 60th anniversary of the passing of musician, singer and composer Solomon Popoli Linda (1909-1962), also known as Solomon Ntsele, who is best known as the composer of the song, “Mbube”.
tgt: Morero o hlompha matswalo a bo 60 a go hlokofala ga rammino, seopedi le motšweletši Solomon Popoli Linda (1901-1962), yoo a tsebegago gape bjalo ka Solomon Ntsele, yoo a tsebegago kudu bjalo ka motšweletši wa koša ya, “Mbube”.

src: 2022 World Maritime Day Parallel Event South Africa will be hosting the 2022 World Maritime Day Parallel Event in Durban from 12 to 14 October 2022.
tgt: Moletlo wa go Lebana wa Letšatši la Dikepe la 2022.

src: The event will be hosted during the OTM, which will also form part of raising awareness of our maritime sector.
tgt: Moletlo o tla swarwa nakong ya OTM, woo le wona e tla bago karolo ya go godiša tsebo ya lekala la rena la dikepe.

src: The event will bring delegates from various countries who will experience the South African maritime industry.
tgt: Moletlo o tla tliša baemedi go tšwa dinageng tša go fapana bao ba tla itemogelang intasteri ya dikepe ya Afrika Borwa.

src: South Africa has been a member of the International Maritime Organization since 1995, which is a specialised agency of the UN responsible for regulating shipping.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e bile leloko la Mokgatlo wa Dikepe wa Boditšhabatšhaba go tloga ka 1995, woo o lego mokgatlo wa go ikgetha wa UN wa go laola dikepe.

src: Tourism Month.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Boeti.

src: Tourism Month is this year being celebrated under the theme of World Tourism Day (27 September) of “Rethinking Tourism”.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Boeti ngwaga wo e ketekwa ka fase ga morero wa Letšatši la Boeti la Lefase (27 Lewedi) wa “Nagana gape ka Boeti”.

src: Domestic tourism is critical in the recovery of the tourism sector, which contributes greatly to the South African GDP and job creation.
tgt: Boeti bja gae bo bohlokwa kudu mo go tsošološeng lekala la boeti, leo le kgathago tema kudu go GDP ya Afrika Borwa le go hlola mošomo.

src: Cabinet is pleased that the hospitality sector has recorded an increase in visitors post the COVID-19 period.
tgt: Kabinete e thabišwa ke gore lekala la kamogelo ya baeti le begile kgolo ya baeti ka morago ga nako ya COVID-19.

src: The million domestic trips taken in the first half of 2022 recorded a 114% increase when compared to the same period in 2021.
tgt: Go tšerwe maeto a gae a milione mo seripeng sa mathomo sa 2022 e begile koketšego ya 114% ge go bapetšwa le nako ya go swana ka 2021.

src: This showed a marked improvement for the same period in 2019, which saw million domestic trips taken.
tgt: Se se bontšha kaonafalo ya mmaraka ya nako ya go swana ka 2019, yeo e bonego maeto ao a tšerwego a gae a milione.

src: As part of celebrating Tourism Month, Cabinet encourages South Africans to undertake ‘Shotleft’ tours to our various provinces.
tgt: Bjalo ka karolo ya go keteka Kgwedi ya Boeti, Kabinete e hlohleletša maAfrika Borwa go tšea maeto a ‘Shortleft’ go ya diprofense tša rena tša go fapana.

src: Cabinet also welcomed the decision by Air Belgium to fly seasonal flights to South Africa, starting from this month (September), which will boost tourism and further cement our status as a tourism destination of choice.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela gape sephetho sa Air Belgium go fofiša difofane tša sehla go ya Afrika Borwa, go thoma kgwedi yona ye (Lewedi), seo se tla matlafatšago boeti gomme sa tiišetša maemo a rena bjalo ka nepo ya boeti ya kgetho.

src: It will include weekly flights to Cape Town and Johannesburg.
tgt: Se tla akaretša difofane tša beke ye nngwe le ye nngwe go ya Motsekapa le Johannesburg.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetša.

src: CongratulationsCabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to: President William Samoei Ruto of the Republic of Kenya, who was inaugurated on Tuesday, 13 September 2022, following peaceful national elections held on 9 August 2022.
tgt: DitebogišoKabinete e lebogiša le go lakaletša tše dibotse go:Mopresidente William Samoei Ruto wa Repabliki ya Kenya, yoo a hlomamišitšwego ka Labobedi, 13 Lewedi 2022, go latela dikgetho tša bosetšhaba tša khutšo tšeo di swerwego ka la 9 Phato 2022.

src: Deputy President David Mabuza attended the inauguration on behalf of President Ramaphosa, and the government and people of the Republic of South Africa.
tgt: Motlatšamopresidente David Mabuza o tsenetše tlhomamišo legatong la Mopresidente Ramaphosa, le mmušo le batho ba Repabliki ya Afrika Borwa.

src: The South African Rugby Union and the City of Cape Town for successfully hosting the eighth edition of the Rugby World Cup Sevens tournament between 9 and 11 September 2022.
tgt: South African Rugby Union le Toropokgolo ya Motsekapa go swara phadišano ya bo seswai ya Rugby World Cup Sevens gare ga 9 le 11 Lewedi 2022.

src: This was the first time that this prestigious event was hosted by an African country and the many thousands of fans who attended were treated to a feast of rugby and South Africa’s renowned hospitality.
tgt: E be e le lekga la mathomo tiragalo ye ye bohlokwa e swarwa ke naga ya Afrika gomme barati ba diketekete bao ba e tsenetšego ba ilwe ba thabišwa ka dijo tša rugby le kamogelo ye e lemogwago ya Afrika Borwa.

src: Condolences Cabinet expressed condolences to the families and friends of: the 18 schoolchildren and two adults who died in a horrific accident in Pongola, KwaZulu-Natal on Friday, 16 September 2022 after an articulated truck collided head-on with a bakkie transporting the learners.
tgt: MahlokoKabinete e romela melaetša ya mahloko go malapa le bagwera ba:Bana ba sekolo ba 18 le batho ba bagolo ba babedi bao ba hlokofetšego mo kotsing ye šoro ka Pongola, KwaZulu-Natal ka Labohlano, 16 Lewedi 2022 ka morago ga go thulana ga lori le bene yeo e bego e nameditše bana ba sekolo.

src: Appointments.
tgt: Bao ba Thwetšwego Mešomong.

src: All appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Batho ka moka bao ba thwetšwego mešomong mangwalo a bona a dithuto a tla tiišetšwa le go netefatšwa ka maleba.

src: a. Mr Makgothi Samuel Thobakgale as Director-General (DG): National Commissioner of the Department of Correctional Services.
tgt: a. Morena Makgothi Samuel Thobakgale bjalo ka Molaodimogolophethiši (DG): Mokhomišinare wa Setšhaba wa Kgoro ya Ditirelo tša Tshokollo.

src: b. Dr Malixole Percival Mahlati as Deputy DG: Hospitals Tertiary Health Services and Human Resources Development at the Department of Health.
tgt: b. Ngaka Malixole Percival Mahlati bjalo ka Motlatšamolaodimogolophethiši (DDG: lefapheng la go šoma ka merero ya Dikolo tša Maokelo tša Thuto ya Godimo ka moka le ya Tlhabollo ya Bašomi mo Kgorong ya Maphelo.

src: c. Mr Siyabonga Blessing Mdubeki as Chief Surveyor-General at the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development.
tgt: c. Morena Siyabonga Blessing Mdubeki bjalo ka Mohlahlobimogolophethiši mo Kgorong ya Temo, Tsošološo ya Naga le Tlhabollo ya Dinagamagaed.

src: d. Mr Phaswa Phineas Mamogale as Chief Financial Officer at the Department of Health.
tgt: Morena Phaswa Phineas Mamogale bjalo ka Mohlankedimogolo wa Ditšhelete mo Kgorong ya Maphelo.

src: Cabinet concurred with the following appointments:a. Mr Tshediso Matona as Commissioner of the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Commission.
tgt: Kabinete e dumelelana le go thwalwa ga batho ba mešomong:a. Morena Tshediso Matona bjalo ka Mokhomišinare wa Khomišene ya Matlafatšo ya Ekonomi ya Bathobaso ka Kakaretšo.

src: Water security.
tgt: Tšhireletšego ya Meetse.

src: Cabinet thanked South Africans for adhering to water restrictions implemented in certain parts of Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni to stabilise the capacity of reservoirs.
tgt: Kabinete e lebogile MaAfrika Borwa ka moka ge ba obametše taelo ya go fokotšwa ga meetse ye phethagaditšwego dikarolong tše dingwe tša Johannesburg, Tshwane le Ekurhuleni go boetša sekeng maemo a matamo.

src: Dams and reservoirs remain under pressure due to high temperatures in Gauteng, and increasing demand forced Rand Water to reduce water supply to municipalities drastically.
tgt: Matamo ka mehutahuta a ka fase ga kgatelelo ye kgolo kudu ka baka la dithemphereitšha tša go fiša tšhiritšhiri gola Gauteng, ebile nyakego ye golelago godimo ya meetse a gapeleditše Rand Water go fokotša ka bontši meetse ao a abelwago mebasepala.

src: The water utility supplies bulk potable water to more than 11 million people in Gauteng, parts of Mpumalanga, the Free State and North West.
tgt: Rand Water e aba meetse a go nwega a mantši bathong ba go feta 11 milione go la Gauteng, dikarolong tše dingwe tša Mpumalanga, Freistata le Leboa Bodikela.

src: These unavoidable restrictions aim to secure water supply and will remain in place until the situation improves.
tgt: Tšona diphokotšo tše tša go se efogege di nepile go boloka kabo ya meetse ebile di tla dula di le gona go ba go fihlela ge seemo se kaonafala.

src: Cabinet called on the public to continue adhering to the water restrictions and play their part by using this scarce resource sparingly.
tgt: Kabinete e dirile boipiletšo setšhabeng go tšwelapele go obamela magato a phokotšo ya meetse le go kgatha tema ya bona ka go a šomiša ka tshwanelo ka ge e le sedirišwa sa go hlokwa kudu.

src: Cabinet welcomed the three-year wage deal reached between Transnet and the United National Transport Union (UNTU), which is applicable for the period 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2025.
tgt: Mogwanto wa Transnet Kabinete e amogetše kwano ya meputso ya mengwaga ye meraro ye kwanetšwego ke Transnet le Yunione ya Mohlakanelwa ya Bosetšhaba ya Dinamelwa (UNTU), ye e tlo dirišwago pakeng ya 1 Moranang 2022 go fihla ka la 31 Hlakola 2025.

src: The Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration mediated this deal, which ended the current industrial action by members of UNTU with immediate effect.
tgt: Khomišene ya Poelano, Bonamodi le Ditherišano e namotše kwano ye, gomme magato a bona a dirile gore boipelaetšo ka maloko a UNTU bo fedišwe ka ponyo ya leihlo.

src: Cabinet also welcomed the decision by the South African Transport and Allied Workers Union to call off the strike.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše gape sephetho sa go fediša mogwanto ka Yunione ya Dinamelwa ya Afrika Borwa le ya Bašomi.

src: Cabinet welcomed the commitment by Transnet to focus on clearing backlogs that occurred across the port and rail system during the industrial action, which negatively impacted the economy and sectors that are dependent on its services.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše boikgafo bja Transnet bja go bea šedi godimo ga go fediša ditšhalelomorago tše bilego gona go ralala boemakepe le dipeakanyong tša ditimela nakong ya magato a boipelaetšo, ao a bilego le seabe se se mpe ikonoming le makaleng ao a tshepetšego godimo ga Transnet go aba ditirelo.

src: Cabinet expressed its gratitude to the support and cooperation given by business during the strike.
tgt: Kabinete e bontšhitše tebogo ya yona godimo ga thekgo le tšhomišanommogo ye laeditšwego ke dikgwebo ka nako ya mogwanto.

src: It encourages a continuous relationship between Transnet management and labour for the benefit of the company and the economy of the country.
tgt: E hlohleletša kamano ye sa felego magareng ga balaodi ba Transnet le bašomi gore khamphani ye le ikonomi ya naga ka bophara di holege.

src: Cabinet welcomed the successful Working Visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by President Cyril Ramaphosa on 15 and 16 October 2022.
tgt: Dikamano tša Afrika Borwa le Saudi Arabia Kabinete e amogetše Ketelo ya Mošomo ye atlegilego ya go ya kua the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia ka Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa ka la 15 le 16 Diphalane 2022.

src: During the visit, the two countries signed 17 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) in various fields such as agriculture, fisheries, mining, renewable energy, security, transport and aquaculture.
tgt: Nakong ya keteko ye, dinaga tše ka bobedi di saenetše Dimemorantamo tše 17 tša Kwešišano go magoro a go fapafapana a go swana le temo, boreatlhapi, meepo, enetši ya go mpšhafatšega, tšhireletšego, dinamelwa le temo ya diphedi le dimela tša ka meetseng.

src: Other MoUs signed are on the establishment of a Joint Business Council, cooperation in the field of military industries and procurements, and on geological survey cooperation.
tgt: Dimemorantamo tše dingwe tša kwešišano tšeo di saenetšwego ke tša mabapi le go hlongwa ga Khansele ya Mohlakanelwa ya Dikgwebo, tšhomišano legorong la diintasteri tša sešole le dithekišetšano, tšhomišano ya ditekolonyakišišo tša thutaswika.

src: The President used the visit to invite Saudi Arabia businesses to South Africa’s fifth investment conference that will be held in 2023.
tgt: Mopresidente o šomišitše ketelo ye go mema dikgwebo tša Saudi Arabia go iponagatša khonferenseng ya bohlano ya dipeeletšo ya Afrika Borwa ye tlo swarwago ka 2023.

src: Saudi Arabia is South Africa’s second largest trading partner in the Middle East and the largest source of imports from the region.
tgt: Saudi Arabia ke mogwebišani wa bobedi wo mogologolo wa Afrika Borwa seleteng sa Bohlabelagare ebile ke mothopo wo mogologolo wa diromelwa ka nageng go tšwa go sona selete se.

src: International relations between both countries have resulted in a positive effect on trade and investment trends.
tgt: Dikamano tša boditšhabatšhaba magareng ga dinaga tše ka bobedi di bile le ditlamorago tše botse godimo ga ditlwaedi tša kgwebišano le dipeeletšo.

src: Infrastructure investment.
tgt: Dipeeletšo tša Mananeokgoparara.

src: Cabinet welcomed the commissioning of a state-of-the-art plastics production plant by leading international manufacturer, the ALPLA Group, at Lanseria in Gauteng.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše go thongwa ga polante ya tšweletšo ya plastiki ya maemo a godimodimo lefaseng ka khampani ya go dira plastiki yeo e tšwago pele maemong a boditšhabatšhaba, ya go bitšwa ALPLA Group, go la Lanseria kua Gauteng.

src: This augments President Ramaphosa’s commitment to position infrastructure development as a means to stimulate the economy and increase employment.
tgt: Se se tlaleletša maikgafo a Mopresidente Ramaphosa a go bea sekeng tlhabollo ya mananeokgoparara bjalo ka mokgwa wa go hlohleletša kgolo ya ikonomi le go atiša mešomo.

src: The investment worth US$50 million is a key contribution to the Lanseria Smart City masterplan that will drive sustainability and recycling as well as create and sustain 350 jobs.
tgt: Dipeeletšo tša boleng bja US$50 milione di kgatha tema ye kgolo godimo ga Leanolegolo la Toropo ya Mabonwa ya Lanseria leo le tlo hlohleletšago seemo seo se tieletšego le tšhomišoleswa le gape go hlola le go šireletša mešomo ye 350.

src: Included is an apprenticeship programme for 36 mechatronics and recycling technicians for ALPLA Group operations across southern Africa.
tgt: Godimo ga dipeeletšo tše go akaretšwa le lenaneo la go ithutela mošomo la batsebi ba 36 ba bointšineere bja dikgerekgere le ba tšhomišogape ba ditiro tša ALPLA Group go ralala selete sa Borwa bja Afrika.

src: The apprentice programme will commence in 2023, with the first 12 South African apprentices coming from local communities.
tgt: Lenaneo le la boithutelamošomo le tlo thoma ka 2023, ka baithutelamošomo ba mathomo ba 12 ba MaAfrika Borwa ba go tšwa mafelong a ka mo nageng.

src: Illegal mining.
tgt: Meepo ye Sego Molaong.

src: Illegal mining hurts communities and our economy, and results in a loss of revenue for both government and the mining sector.
tgt: Meepo ye sego molaong e kweša setšhaba bohloko le go gobatša ikonomi ya gaborena, ebile dipoelo tša yona ke tobo ya letseno go bobedi mmušo le lefapha la meepo.

src: Cabinet welcomed the seizure of a firearms cache and the arrest of 20 suspects linked to illegal mining during an operation at a mineshaft in Stilfontein in North West.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše go amogwa ga dithunya tšeo di bego di utilwe le go golegwa ga bagononelwa ba 20 ba go amana le meepo ye sego molaong ka nako ya lesolophuruphutšo kua mokoting wa moepo wa Stilfontein go la Leboa Bodikela.

src: Cabinet appeals to South Africans to continue working with law-enforcement agencies to ensure the success of future anti-crime operations.
tgt: Kabinete e dira boipiletšo go MaAfrika Borwa go tšwelapele go šomišana le mabotho a phethagatšo ya molao go netefatša go atlega ga masolo a kamoso a twantšho ya bosenyi.

src: This will send a strong message that crime does not pay, and that criminals will be arrested and prosecuted without fear or favour.
tgt: Se se tla romela molaetša wo bogale wa gore bosenyi ga bo thuše ka selo, le gore badirabosenyi ba tlo golegwa le go sekišwa ntle poifo goba go šokelwa.

src: Energy Eskom recently signed 30-year lease agreements with four independent power producer investors to construct new clean-energy generation capacity at Majuba and Tutuka power stations in Mpumalanga.
tgt: Enetši Eskom e saenetše dikwanelo tša go hiriša tša mengwaga ye 30 gotee le babeeletši ba bane ba batšweletši ba go ikema ba mohlagase go aga metšhene ye mefsa ya go fehla enetši ya go hlweka kua ditišing tša mohlagase tša Majuba le Tutuka gola Mpumalanga.

src: The land leases will attract an estimated investment of about R40 billion.
tgt: Khirišo ye ya seripa sa naga e tla goketša dipeeletšo tše phopholeditšwego tša go batamela R40 bilione.

src: The four investors – HDF Energy South Africa, Red Rocket SA, Sola Group and Mainstream Renewable Power Developments South Africa – will contribute at least 2 000 megawatts to the national electricity grid.
tgt: Babeeletši ba ba bane – HDF Energy South Africa, Red Rocket SA, Solar Group le Mainstream Renewable Power Developments South Africa – ba tlo fehla mohlagase wa go lekana dimekawate tše 2 000 godimo ga mohlagase wa go tšweletšwa setšhabeng.

src: The new generation capacity is expected to be connected to the grid within 24 to 36 months from financial closure, subject to environmental, land zoning and other regulatory approvals.
tgt: Phehlo ye ye mpsha ya mohlagase go letetšwe gore e kgokaganywe le mohlagase wo o tšweletšwago nageng ka bophara mo dikgweding tše 24 go fihla go tše 36 go tloga ge ngwaga wo wa ditšhelete o fela, ka go latela ditumelelo tša tikologo, tša karolo ya mafelo le tše dingwe tša taolo.

src: Food security.
tgt: Tšhireletšego ya Dijo.

src: Cabinet welcomed the hosting of the Agri SA Congress 2022 in Pretoria on 13 and 14 October 2022 under the theme: “Growing Local”.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetše go swarwa ka mo nageng ga Lekgotla la 2022 la Agri SA go la Pretoria ka la 13 le la 14 Diphalane 2022 ka fase ga morero wo: “Kgodišo ya Tšweletšo ya ka Nageng”.

src: The congress engaged on issues such as making agriculture masterplans work for local growers sustainable infrastructure for locally grown food making the local environment sustainable for local food production into the future, and strengthening food producers’ capacity to process locally grown produce.
tgt: Lekgotla le le rerišane ka merero ya go swana le go dira gore maanakgolo a temo a šomele batšweletši ba ka mo nageng mananeokgoparara a go swarelela a dijo tša go tšweletšwa ka mo nageng go dira gore tikologo ya ka mo nageng e tšee nako ye telele godimo ga tšweletšo ya dijo ya ka mo nageng le ka bokamosong, le go matlafatša mabokgoni a tšweletšo ya dijo go diriša ditšweletšo tšeo di tšweleditšwego ka mo nageng.

src: In further prioritising food security, Cabinet also welcomed the launch of the National Biosecurity Hub, by the Department of Science and Innovation's Agricultural Bio-economy Innovation Partnership Programme, in collaboration with the University of Pretoria.
tgt: Ka gona go bea pele tšhireletšego ya dijo kamoso, Kabinete e amogetše go tsebagatšwa ga Hapo ya Bosetšhaba ya Tšhireletšego ya Tlhago, ka Kgoro ya Saense le Lenaneo la Kgwebišano ya Temo ya Ikonomi ya Diphedi, ka tšhomišano le Yunibesithi ya Pretoria.

src: The hub will support the prevention, reduction and management of crop and animal disease, which will contribute to increased productivity, food security and sustainable rural development.
tgt: Hapo ye e tla thekga thibelo, phokotšo le taolo ya dipuno le malwetši a diphoofolo, ao a tlo bago le seabe sa tšweletšo ye hlatlogetšego godimo, tšhireletšego ya dijo le tlhabollo ye swarelelago ya dinagamagae.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diphetho tša Kabinete.

src: Ratification of the Decentralisation Charter of the African Union (AU).
tgt: Go Dumelelwa ga Tšhatha ya Kopano ya Afrika (AU) ya go Hlongwa ga Makala.

src: Cabinet approved the submission to Parliament the AU Charter on the Values and Principles of Decentralisation, Local Governance and Local Development for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše tlhagišo Palamenteng ga Tšhatha ya AU ka Mehola le Metheo ya go Hlongwa ga Makala, Pušoselegae le Tlhabollo ya ka Nageng gore e dumelelwe.

src: South Africa signed the charter in August 2021.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e saenetše tšhatha ye ka Phato 2021.

src: The Decentralisation Charter provides a framework to all member states a guiding document on the decentralisation of powers and functions from national to other spheres of government.
tgt: Tšhatha ye ya go Hlongwa ga Makala e fana ka tlhako go mebušo ka moka ye lego maloko ka sengwalwa sa tlhahlo ka khuetšo ya go hlongwa ga makala le mehola ya ona go tloga mmušong wa bosetšhaba go ya didikong tše dingwe tša mmušo.

src: The charter deals largely with the decentralisation of authority and functions, local governance framework and local development.
tgt: Tšhatha ye e swaragane kudu le phatlalatšo ya taolo le mehola, tlhako ya pušo le tlhabollo ya ka mo nageng.

src: 32nd Annual International Railway Safety Council (IRSC).
tgt: Khansele ya bo-32 ya Ngwaga ka Ngwaga ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya Polokego ya Ditimela (IRSC).

src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the 32nd Annual IRSC Meeting in Johannesburg from 1 to 6 October 2023 under the theme: “Reshaping railways in an uncertain World”.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše go swarwa ga Kopano ya bo-32 ya Ngwaga ka Ngwaga ya IRSC gola Johannesburg go thoma ka la 1 go fihla ka la 6 Diphalane 2023 ka fase ga morero wo: “Phetošo ya sebopego sa ditimela mo Lefaseng leo go sa tsebjego tša kamoso”.

src: The IRSC is an international forum that brings together railway safety professionals from all over the world to exchange experiences so as to improve railway safety.
tgt: IRSC ke foramo ya boditšhabatšhaba ya go kopantšha mmogo ditsebi tša polokego ya ditimela go tšwa lefaseng ka bophara go fana maitemogelo go kaonafatša polokego ya ditimela.

src: As a member of the IRSC, South Africa’s Railway Safety Regulator last hosted this forum in Draft National Infrastructure Plan 2050 (NIP 2050) Phase Cabinet approved the gazetting of the draft NIP 2050 Phase 2 for public consultation.
tgt: Bjalo ka leloko la IRSC, Kemedi ya Afrika Borwa ya Polokego ya Ditimela e swere foramo ye la mafelelo ka Seakanywa sa Leano la Bosetšhaba sa Mananeokgoparara a 2050 (NIP 2050) Kgato ya Kabinete e dumeletše phatlalatšo kuranteng ya mmušo ya Kgato ya Bobedi ya seakanywa sa NIP sa 2050 gore setšhaba se fe ditshwayotshwayo tša sona.

src: The plan offers direction in strengthening and augmenting government strategic integrated projects.
tgt: Leano le le fa tlhahlo matlafatšong le kaonafatšong ya diprotšeke tše logetšwego maano tša mmušo tša mohlakanelwa.

src: It identifies the strategic projects in human settlements municipal electricity water solid waste passenger transport education and health infrastructure digital infrastructure, and crime and corruption.
tgt: Seakanywa se se hlaola diprotšeke tše logetšwego maano madulong a batho mohlagase wa mmasepala meetse dilahlwa tše thata dinamelwa tša banamedi thuto le mananeokgoparara a maphelo mananeokgoparara a titšithale, le bosenyi le bomenetša.

src: The format of the plan provides a vision of the area to be tackled, offers an assessment of the current status, outlines the essential conditions for success and states what needs to be done to achieve the vision.
tgt: Sebopego sa leano le se fana ka ponelopele ya fao go swanetšego go fiwa šedi, se fana ka phetleko ya seemo sa bjale, se hlatholla dipeelano tše bohlokwa tša go atlega le go bolela gore go swanetše gore go dirwe eng go fihlelela ponelopele ye.

src: It proposes the implementation process to be taken over the three-year running cycle action plan.
tgt: Se šišinya tshepedišo ya phethagatšo ye swanetšego go latelwa mo leanong la magato la go gagaba tekano ya mengwaga ye meraro.

src: National Implementation Framework towards the Profssionalisation of the Public Service Cabinet approved the National Implementation Framework towards the Profssionalisation of the Public Service.
tgt: Tlhako ya Phethagatšo ya Bosetšhaba ya go Fihlelela Bokgoni Ditirelong tša Mmušo Kabinete e dumeletše Tlhako ya Phethagatšo ya Bosetšhaba ya go fihlelela Bokgoni Ditirelong tša Mmušo.

src: The framework was published for public consultation in 2021.
tgt: Tlhako ye e phatlaladitšwe ka 2021 gore setšhaba se ntšhe sa mafahleng a sona.

src: The framework provides five pillars on interventions in professionalising the Public Service.
tgt: Tlhako ye e fana ka maikokotlelo a mahlano mo magatong a go hloma bokgoni Ditirelong tša Mmušo.

src: The pillars include pre-entry recruitment and selection within the Public Service induction and onboarding planning and performance management continuous learning and professional development, and career progression and career incidents.
tgt: Metheo ye ya boikokotlelo e akaretša kgoketšo ya pele o tsena le tlhokolo mo Ditirelong tša Mmušo kgakolo le tlwaetšo thulaganyo le taolo ya bodiragatši thuto ye tšwelagopele, kgatelopele ya kgetho ya mošomo le ditiragalo tša mabapi le kgetho ya mošomo.

src: Changes in the conditions of employment for Directors-General (DGs).
tgt: Diphetogo ka Gare ga Dipeelano tša Mošomo tša Balaodipharephare (di-DG).

src: Cabinet approved the report that proposes measures to strengthen the capacity and capability of the DGs in the Public Service.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše pego ya go šišinya magato a go matlafatša mabokgoni le bokgoni bja Balaodipharephare (di-DG) Ditirelong tša Mmušo.

src: The report made several proposals, including the tenure of DGs and the management of delegations by the Executive Authority to the accounting officers.
tgt: Pego ye e dirile ditšhišinyo tše mmalwa, go akaretšwa le paka ya ka kantorong ya di-DG le taolo ya baromiwa ka Lekgotlaphethiši go bahlankedi ba taolo.

src: The report also proposed that the DG in The Presidency will be designated as the Head of Public Administration.
tgt: Pego ye e šišintše gape le gore Molaodipharephare Kantorong ya Mopresidente o tla neelwa Hlogo ya Ditirelo tša Mmušo.

src: In the provinces, this function will be designated to the DGs in the offices of the Premiers.
tgt: Kua diprofenseng, mošomo wo o tla neelwa Balaodipharephare dikantorong tša Ditonakgolo.

src: The report further proposed measures to guide departments on the management of contracts of DGs.
tgt: Pego ye e šišintše gape le magato a go hlahla dikgoro ka taolo ya dikontraka le Balaodipharephare.

src: The revised Performance Management System for DGs is being revised to align it with the approved changes.
tgt: Peakanyo ye Fetlekilwego ya Taolo ya Bodiragatši go Balaodipharephare e gare e ya fetlekwa gore e gate ka mošito o tee le diphetogo tšeo di dumeletšwego.

src: The Acting Minister of Public Service and Administration, Mr Thulas Nxesi, will next week convene a media briefing to outline the National Implementation Framework towards the Profssionalisation of the Public Service and also unpack the approved changes in the conditions of employment for DGs.
tgt: Tona ya Motšwaoswere ya Ditirelo tša Mmušo le Tsamaišo, Ntate Thulas Nxesi, o tlare mo bekeng ye tlago a sware kopano ya tshedimošetšo ya babegaditaba go hlatholla Tlhako ya Bosetšhaba ya Phethagatšo go fihlelela Bokgoni Ditirelong tša Mmušo le gape go hlatholla gabotse diphetogo tše dumeletšwego dipeelanong tša go thwalwa ga Balaodipharephare.

src: Fifth Progress Report on the Implementation of the White Paper on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (WPRPD) 2020-2021.
tgt: Pego ya Bohlano ya Mošomo ka Phethagatšo ya Sengwalwa sa Makgoraditsela ka Ditokelo tša Batho ba go Phela ka Bogole (WPRPD) 2020-2021.

src: Cabinet approved the Fifth Progress Report on the Implementation of the WPRPD, which provides an update on the implementation of the WPRPThe report covers inputs from national and provincial government departments.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše Pego ya Bohlano ya Mošomo ka phethagatšo ya WPRPD, yeo e fanago ka seemo sa bjale ka phethagatšo ya WPRPPego ye e akaretša le ditshwayotshwayo go tšwa dikgorong tša mmušo tša bosetšhaba le tša profense.

src: It provides updates on the policy implementation that include budget allocations.
tgt: E fana ka seemo sa bjale ka phethagatšo ya pholisi ye akaretšago diriparipana tša ditekanyetšokabo.

src: The first annual progress report was published in 2017.
tgt: Pego ya mathomo ya seemo sa mošomo ya ngwaga ka ngwaga e phatlaladitšwe ka 2017.

src: This fifth progress report has been approved to be gazetted and published by the Department of Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities.
tgt: Pego ye ya bohlano e dumeletšwe go gatišwa kuranteng ya mmušo le go phatlalatšwa ke Kgoro ya Basadi, Baswa le Batho ba go Phela ka Bogole.

src: Amendment to Article 20(1) of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW).
tgt: Phetošo ya Athikele ya 20(1) ya Kopano ya Phedišo ya Mehuta ka Moka ya Kgethollo Kgahlanong le Basadi (CEDAW).

src: Cabinet approved the submission to Parliament of the amendment to Article 20(1) of the CEDAW for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše tlhagišo Palamenteng ya Phetošo ya Athikele 20(1) ya CEDAW gore e dumelelwe.

src: The amendments provide for an increased duration of the committee meetings that process the member states’ reports.
tgt: Diphetošo tše di fana ka nako ye teletšana ya dikopano tša komiti tša go lebelela dipego tša mebušo ye lego maloko.

src: South Africa signed this convention in 1993 and subsequently ratified it in December 1995.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e saenetše kwano ye ka 1993 le go e dumelela moragonyana ga fao ka Manthole 1995.

src: The submission to Parliament seeks to align the previously ratified convention with the amendment to Article 20(1) of the convention.
tgt: Tlhagišo ye Palamenteng e šetšane le go tsamaiša ka mošito o tee kwano ye e dumeletšwego kua morago gotee le phetošo ya Athikele 20(1) ya kwano ye.

src: Global Convention on the Recognition of Qualifications concerning Higher Education Cabinet approved the submission to Parliament of the Global Convention on the Recognition of Qualifications concerning Higher Education for ratification.
tgt: Kwano ya Lefase ka Bophara ka Kamogelo ya Mangwalo a Thuto Mabapi le Thuto ya Godingwana.

src: Once ratified it will be deposited to the United Nations (UN) Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization and domestically enabled through the National Qualifications Framework Act, 2008 (Act 67 of 2008).
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše tlhagišo Palamenteng ya Kwano ya Lefase ka Bophara ka Kamogelo ya Mangwalo a Thuto mabapi le Thuto ya Godingwana gore e dumelelwe.

src: The Global Convention establishes universal principles for fair, transparent and non-discriminatory recognition of higher education qualifications and qualifications.
tgt: Ge e šetše e dumeletšwe e tla romelwa Mokgatlong wa Ditšhabakopano (UN) wa Thuto, Saenthefiki le tša Setšo le go kgontšhwa go šoma ka mo nageng ka Molao wa Bosetšhaba wa Tlhako ya Mangwalo a Thuto, 2008 (Molao 67 wa 2008).

src: It allows for the recognition of foreign qualifications in 193 UN member states.
tgt: E dumelela temogo ya mangwalo a thuto a dinagašele mo mebušo ye 193 ye lego maloko a UKgogelomorago ya Diphetošo tša Tlhahli ya Maloko a Komitiphethiši.

src: Withdrawal of the amendments to the Guide for Members of the Executive.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše kwalakwatšo ye kwalakwaditšwego ke Kantoro ya Mopresidente ka Mošupologo, 17 Diphalane 2022 go gogelamorago diphetošo tšeo di dirilwego go Tlhahli ya Maloko a Komitiphethiši, yeo e bitšwago Pukukgakollo ya Ditona, ya 2022.

src: Cabinet endorsed the announcement made by The Presidency on Monday, 17 October 2022 to withdraw the amendments made to the Guide for Members of the Executive, also called the Ministerial Handbook, for 2022.
tgt: Diphetošo tše di dirilwego ka Moranang 2022 di fane ka thekgo ya tlaleletšo go tše dingwe tša dikantoro tša Ditona tšeo di rwelego maikarabelo a lefapha la go feta le tee.

src: The amendments that were made in April 2022 provided for additional capacity to some of the offices of the Ministers who are responsible for more than one portfolio.
tgt: Diphetošo tše di be di nyaka gore Mmušo o rwale maikarabelo ka botlalo a disenyegelo tša go amana le kabo ya mohlagase le meetse madulong a semmušo a go dulwa ke maloko a komitiphethiši.

src: They also required the State to take over full responsibility for the costs associated with the provision of electricity and water to official residences occupied by members of the executive.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile dipelaelo tšeo di hlagišitšwego ke maloko a setšhaba ebile e tšeere sephetho sa go sekaseka Tlhahli ya Maloko a Komitiphethiši.

src: This process will be handled by a neutral structure and once completed, the guide will be made public through the Department of Public Service and Administration’s website: WEBTOKEJust Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) and JETP Investment Plan (JETP-IP).
tgt: Tshepedišo ye e šogašogwa ke setheo sa go se tšee lehlakore ebile ge e fihlile mafelelong, tlhahli ye e tlo phatlalatšwa setšhabeng ka wepsaete ye ya Kgoro ya Ditirelo tša Mmušo le Tsamaišo: WEBTOKEKgwerano Diphetogong tša Enetši tša go se Tšee Lehlakore (JETP) le Leano la Dipeeletšo la JETP (JETP-IP).

src: After welcoming a presentation on the JETP and the JETP-IP, Cabinet endorsed the JETP-IP and expressed its appreciation of the detailed work undertaken to develop it.
tgt: Ka morago ga go amogela tlhagišo ka JETP le JETP-IP, Kabinete e thekgile ka atla pedi J ETP-IP le go laetša ka fao e kgotsofetšego ka gona ka mošomo wa go tsenelela wo o dirilwego go e kaonafatša.

src: The JETP-IP outlines the investments required to achieve the decarbonisation commitments made by the Government of South Africa while promoting sustainable development, and ensuring a just transition for affected workers and communities.
tgt: JETP-IP e hlatholla dipeeletšo tšeo di nyakegago go fihlelela maikgafo a go fediša khabone ao a dirilwego ke Mmušo wa Afrika Borwa mola ka go le lengwe go hlohleletšwa tlhabollo ya go swarelela nako ye teletšana, le go netefatša gore go fihlelelwa diphetogo tša go se tšee lehlakore go bašomedi bao ba amegago le setšhaba.

src: The Inter-Ministerial Committee on Climate Change will soon hold a media briefing to provide more details.
tgt: Komiti ya Magareng ga Ditona ka Phetogo ya Klaemete e tlare go se goye kae ya swara tshedimošetšo le babegaditaba go fana ka tshedimošo ka botlalo.

src: Bills.
tgt: Melaokakanywa.

src: Merchant Shipping Bill of 2022.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wa 2022 wa Dinamelwakepe tša Bagwebi.

src: Cabinet has approved the submission of the Merchant Shipping Bill of 2022 to Parliament for further processing.
tgt: Kabinete e dumeletše tlhagišo Palamenteng ya Molaokakanywa wa 2022 wa Dinamelwakepe tša Bagwebi gore o lebelelwe goya pele.

src: The Bill overhauls the 70-year-old Merchant Shipping Act, 1951 (Act 57 of 1951).
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o mpshafatša Molao wa Dinamelwakepe tša Bagwebi wa go ba le mengwaga ye 70 ka bogolo, 1951 (Molao 57 wa 1951).

src: Once enacted, the Bill will provide the merchant shipping legal framework to regulate ships’ value chain.
tgt: Ge o šetše o dumeletšwe, Molaokakanywa wo o tlo fana ka tlhako ya semolao ya dinamelwakepe tša Bagwebi go laola magatokamano a dikepe.

src: It will regulate amongst others the designing, registration, naming and scrapping of ships.
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo, magareng ga tše dingwe, o tla laola tlhamo, boingwadišo, go rea maina le go ntšhwa ga dikepe.

src: These changes will contribute towards reviving the maritime transport sector and also aligning the country with the International Maritime Organisation Convention.
tgt: Diphetošo tše di tlo ba le seabe tsošološong ya lefapha la dinamelwa tša mabopong le go tsamaiša naga ye ka mošito o tee le Kwano ya Mokgatlo wa Boditšhabatšhaba wa tša Mabopo.

src: South Africa has ratified this convention.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e dumeletše kwano ye.

src: Statistics Amendment Bill of 2020 Cabinet approved the submission to Parliament of the Statistics Amendment Bill of 2022 for further processing.
tgt: Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa 2020 wa Dipalopalo Kabinete e dumeletše tlhagišo Palamenteng ya Molaokakanywaphetošwa wa 2022 gore o lebelelwe goya pele.

src: The Bill proposes the amendment to the Statistics Act, 1999 (Act 6 of 1999).
tgt: Molaokakanywa wo o šišinya phetošo ya Molao wa Dipalopalo, 1999 (Molao 6 wa 1999).

src: The amendments provide for the development and implementation of the National Statistics System that supports evidence-based decisions.
tgt: Diphetošo tše di fana ka tlhabollo le phethagatšo ya Peakanyo ya Bosetšhaba ya Dipalopalo yeo e thekgago diphetho tša go ba le bohlatse.

src: They strengthen the existing coordination between Statistics South Africa and other organs of state, and broaden the regulatory framework of the Act.
tgt: Di matlafatša tšhomišano ye lego gona magareng ga Dipalopalo tša Afrika Borwa le ditho tše dingwe tša mmušo, ebile di nabiša tlhako ya taolo ya Molao wo.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Ditiragalo tšeo di Tlago.

src: National Presidential Small, Micro and Medium Enterprises (SMME) and Cooperatives Summit.
tgt: Samiti ya Bosetšhaba ya Lesolo la Mopresidente ka Dikgwebopotlana, tše Nnyane le tša Magareng (di-SMME) le Dikoporasi.

src: The Department of Small Business Development, in partnership with private-sector stakeholders, will host the National Presidential SMME and Cooperatives Summit in Bryanston, Gauteng from 13 to 15 November 2022.
tgt: Kgoro ya Tlhabollo ya Dikgwebo tše Nnyane, ka kgwebišano le bakgathatema ba lefapha la praebete, e tla swara Samiti ya Bosetšhaba ya Lesolo la Mopresidente ka Dikgwebopotlana, tše Nnyane le tša Magareng (di-SMME) le Dikoporasi gola Bryanston, Gauteng go tloga ka la 13 go fihla ka la 15 Dibatsela 2022.

src: The summit will bring together private and public sector key actors in the small enterprise ecosystem, to deliberate on finding ways to collaborate in strengthening this sector.
tgt: Samiti ye e tla kopantšha mmogo bakgathatema ba bohlokwa ba praebete le ba lekala la mmušo ka gare ga peakanyo ya dikgwebo tše nnyane, go rerišana ka go hwetša ditsela tša go šomišana mmogo go matlafatša lefapha le.

src: Expected participants include chambers of commerce, SMME practitioners, academics, policymakers and development finance institutions.
tgt: Bakgathatema bao ba letetšwego ba akaretša lekgotla la dikgwebo, ditsebi tša di-SMME, bahlami ba dipholisi le ditheo tša tlhabollo ya ditšhelete.

src: The summit will also discuss the National Integrated Small Enterprise Development Masterplan, which provides a strategic framework to strengthen the SMME sector.
tgt: Samiti ye e tla rerišana le ka Leanolegolo la Bosetšhaba la Mohlakanelwa la Dikgwebo tše Nnyane, leo le fanago ka tlhako ye logetšwego maano ya go matlafatša lefapha la di-SMMSamiti ye go letetšwe gape gore e tsebagatše Difoka tša Ngwaga ka Ngwaga tša Bosetšhaba tša Mopresidente tša di-SMMGo Swarwa ga Samiti ya bo-2022 ya Dikgaruru tša go Ikala ka Bong le Polao ya Basadi Mopresidente Ramaphosa o tla swara Samiti ya Bobedi ya Mopresidente ya GBVF kua Sentharengkgoparara ya Gallagher gola Gauteng ka la 1 le la 2 Dibatsela 2022.

src: The summit is also expected to introduce the Annual National Presidential SMME Awards.
tgt: Samiti ya mathomo ye bego e swerwe ka 2018 e šomišitšwe go itlama ka boswa ga mmušo le bagwebišani ba leago go fediša ditiragalo tše lego godimo tša dikgaruru kgahlanong le basadi ka mo nageng.

src: Hosting of the Presidential Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Summit 2022 President Ramaphosa will host the second Presidential GBVF Summit at the Gallagher Convention Centre in Gauteng on 1 and 2 November 2022.
tgt: Samiti ya bobedi e tla šomišwa go sekaseka pele kgatelopele ye fihleletšwego ya Leano la Bosetšhaba le Logetšwego Maano ka GBVYona e tlo swarwa ka fase ga morero wo: “Boikarabelo, Potlakišo le Tlaleletšo GONA BJALE”.

src: The first summit held in 2018 was used to recommit government and social partners to ending the high incidents of violence against women in the country.
tgt: Samiti ye e tla rerišana ka, magareng ga tše dingwe, go hwetša mekgwa ya go potlakiša magato le boikarabelo go tšwa dikgorong tše bohlokwa le bakgathatema ka moka ba go akaretša mekgatlo ye lego setšhabeng, lefapha la praebete le bašomi.

src: Fifth Presidential Imbizo to the Northern Cape.
tgt: Imbizo ya Bohlano ya Mopresidente kua Kapa Leboa.

src: The Fifth District Development Model (DDM) Presidential Imbizo in Upington, Northern Cape will take place on Friday, 21 October 2022 at the local Mxolisi Dicky Jacobs Stadium.
tgt: Imbizo ya Mopresidente ya Mmotlolo wa Bohlano wa Tlhabollo ya Dilete (DDM) go la Upington, Kapa Leboa e tla phethagala ka Labohlano, 21 Diphalane 2022 Lepatlelong la fao la Mxolisi Dicky Jacobs Stadium.

src: The DDM Presidential Imbizo will assess service-delivery progress and challenges in the Northern Cape and intervene to resolve them.
tgt: Imbizo ya Mopresidente ya DDM e tlo sekaseka kgatelopele ya kabo ya ditirelo le ditlhotlo tša kua Kapa Leboa le go tsena seemo seo ka bogare go rarolla ditlhotlo tšeo.

src: The DDM ensures that service-delivery planning, implementation and budgeting are integrated to enhance service delivery to communities.
tgt: DDM e netefatša gore thulaganyo ya kabo ya ditirelo, phethagatšo le bolekanyetši e ba monwana le lenala go kaonafatša kabo ya ditirelo bathong.

src: Leading up to the Imbizo, Ministers, members of the executive councils and mayors will embark on community-outreach activities in and around Upington.
tgt: Ka gona go itokišetša Imbizo ye, Ditona, maloko a makgotlaphethiši le dimeyara ba tlo tsenela ditiragalo tša go fihlelela setšhaba ka gare ga Upington le go e potologa.

src: Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) Cabinet believes that the 2022 MTBPS to be tabled by Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana on Wednesday, 26 October 2022 is an important part of South Africa’s open and accountable budgeting process.
tgt: Pego ya Pholisi ya Tekanyetšokabo ya Paka ya Magareng (MTBPS) Kabinete e dumela gore MTBPS ya 2022 yeo e tlo hlagišwago ke Tona ya Ditšhelete Enoch Godongwana ka Laboraro, 26 Diphalane 2022 ke karolo ye bohlokwa ya tshepedišo ya phatlalatša le ya boikarabelo ya bolekanyetši.

src: The MTBPS gives substance to government's commitments within an overall level of spending that the nation can afford.
tgt: MTBPS ke mokgwa wa go phethagatša maikgafo a mmušo ntle le go fetiša magomokakaretšo a disenyegelo ao mmušo o ka a kgonang.

src: It further details how government will close the gap between revenue and expenditure, and make the most of the available resources.
tgt: E hlatholla goya pele ka fao mmušo o tla netefatšago gore disenyegelo ga di fete letseno, le go dira tše ntši ka didirišwa tše lego gona.

src: Matric Exams.
tgt: Ditlhahlobo tša Marematlou.

src: The 2022 National Senior Certificate examinations begin on 31 October and end on 7 December 2022.
tgt: Ditlhahlobo tša 2022 tša Bosetšhaba tša Mphato wa Marematlou di thoma ka la 31 Diphalane le go fela ka la 7 Manthole 2022.

src: Cabinet wishes the Class of 2022 well as they embark on the final leg of their school journey.

src: The Department of Public Service and Administration, in partnership with the National Planning Commission and the University of KwaZulu-Natal School of Development Studies, will host the NDP and State Capacity Conference from 7 to 9 November 2022 at Howard College Campus, University of KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Presidential Summit on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF).

src: Cabinet welcomed the hosting of the second Presidential Summit on GBVF at the Gallagher Estate in Midrand, Gauteng on 1 and 2 November 2022 under the theme: “Accountability, Acceleration and Amplification, NOW!” The summit reflected on progress made in the implementation of declarations proposed during the 2018 Presidential Summit, which reaffirmed the country’s commitment to a united, comprehensive and effective response to GBVParticipants at the two-day summit accounted for work being done towards the implementation of the National Strategic Plan (NSP) on GBVF, which aims to provide a multi-sectoral, coherent strategic policy and programming framework to strengthen a coordinated national response to the crisis of GBVF by the government and country as a whole.
tgt: Cabinet welcomed the hosting of the second Presidential Summit on GBVF at the Gallagher Estate in Midrand, Gauteng on 1 and 2 November 2022 under the theme: “Accountability, Acceleration and Amplification, NOW!” The summit reflected on progress made in the implementation of declarations proposed during the 2018 Presidential Summit, which reaffirmed the country’s commitment to a united, comprehensive and effective response to GBVParticipants at the two-day summit accounted for work being done towards the implementation of the National Strategic Plan (NSP) on GBVF, which aims to provide a multi-sectoral, coherent strategic policy and programming framework to strengthen a coordinated national response to the crisis of GBVF by the government and country as a whole.

src: The summit was the ideal platform to engage in honest and robust discussions around successes and challenges in the fight against GBVIt also showcased the need for collective action and how significant success can be achieved if adequate resources are provided and managed correctly.
tgt: The summit was the ideal platform to engage in honest and robust discussions around successes and challenges in the fight against GBVIt also showcased the need for collective action and how significant success can be achieved if adequate resources are provided and managed correctly.

src: The agreements reached at the summit have demonstrated the importance of the partnership that government has forged with civil society, business, development partners, the faith-based sector and other sectors to work together to deal with the scourge of GBVSome of the interventions agreed upon included the need to allocate adequate funding to the NSP on GBVF, to implement consequence management mechanisms to ensure accountability, and to strengthen national, provincial and local accountability structures.
tgt: The agreements reached at the summit have demonstrated the importance of the partnership that government has forged with civil society, business, development partners, the faith-based sector and other sectors to work together to deal with the scourge of GBVSome of the interventions agreed upon included the need to allocate adequate funding to the NSP on GBVF, to implement consequence management mechanisms to ensure accountability, and to strengthen national, provincial and local accountability structures.

src: Cabinet reiterated that all acts of violence and abuse will not be tolerated in our society.
tgt: Cabinet reiterated that all acts of violence and abuse will not be tolerated in our society.

src: Communities are urged to tackle the scourge of GBVF head-on by reporting perpetrators to law-enforcement agencies.
tgt: Communities are urged to tackle the scourge of GBVF head-on by reporting perpetrators to law-enforcement agencies.

src: Each sector of our society must play its part by creating conditions that make it difficult, if not impossible, for GBVF to thrive.
